definition_zh: 区分；分化；差异化；（数学）微分；分层
definition_en: the act of telling things apart, the process by which things become unlike, or the mathematical operation of finding a derivative
core_image: 一条原本同质的线分成两支：细胞、产品、课程各自长出不同的形状
scene: 显微镜下，一个细胞分裂成两个形状不同的细胞。Under the microscope one cell divides into two cells of different shapes, and the observer writes differentiation in the notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 differentiation 是「分化」（第 1、3 个义项：区辨与生物分化）；句意：显微镜下，一个细胞分裂成两个形状不同的细胞，观察者在记录本上写下「分化」。图中可辨识物件：显微镜、培养皿、两支不同形状的细胞、记录本。

collocations.zh: A 与 B 之间的区分

senses.title: Telling two things apart
senses.definition: the act of recognizing or stating the difference between two or more things
senses.definitionCN: 识别或说明两个或更多事物之间差别的行为
senses.example: The test rewards fine differentiation between closely related species.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试奖励对近缘物种的精细区分。
senses.why: The Latin verb differre meant 'to carry apart'. Differentiation is the mental act of carrying two things apart until the gap between them is visible.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 differre 意为“分开搬运”。differentiation 就是把两样东西在头脑中搬开、直到它们之间的缝隙看得见的行为。

senses.title: The process of becoming unlike
senses.definition: the process by which something develops qualities that separate it from others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 某物发展出使其区别于同类之特性的过程
senses.example: Regional dialects show gradual differentiation over centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 地区方言在数百年间逐渐分化。
senses.why: Here the word names a process rather than an act of judgment. Two things start alike and drift apart; the -ation suffix makes the drift itself the noun.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词命名的不是判断行为，而是一个过程。两样东西起初相似，慢慢漂开；-ation 后缀使这段漂移本身成为名词。

senses.title: Cells taking on special roles
senses.definition: in biology, the process by which a less specialized cell becomes a distinct cell type
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中未特化的细胞变成特定细胞类型的过程
senses.example: Stem cell differentiation produces muscle, nerve and bone cells.
senses.exampleCN: 干细胞分化产生肌肉、神经与骨细胞。
senses.why: A stem cell carries the same instructions as every other cell. Differentiation is what carries one copy of those instructions down a single path, so the cell stops being interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 干细胞携带的指令与其他细胞相同。分化就是把其中一份指令搬上一条特定路径，使这个细胞不再可互换。

senses.title: Making a product stand out
senses.definition: in marketing, the design of a product or brand so that buyers perceive it as distinct from rivals
senses.definitionCN: 营销中把产品或品牌设计得让买家觉得它不同于竞争者
senses.example: The firm relies on differentiation rather than low prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司靠差异化而非低价取胜。
senses.why: The verb differre also means 'to defer, to set apart'. A marketer sets a product apart from the shelf around it, and the noun names that deliberate setting-apart.
senses.whyCN: 动词 differre 也有“推迟、置于一旁”的意思。营销者把产品从四周的货架上“置开”，这个名词就命名这种刻意的分离。

senses.title: Teaching different levels in one class
senses.definition: in education, the adaptation of tasks and materials to learners of different readiness levels
senses.definitionCN: 教育中为不同准备水平的学习者调整任务与材料
senses.example: Curriculum differentiation lets advanced students move ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 分层课程让进度快的学生继续向前。
senses.why: A single class is treated as a set of groups rather than one mass. The word transfers the biological image of branching paths into the classroom.
senses.whyCN: 一个班级被当作一组组人，而不是一团人。这个词把生物学的“分岔路径”意象搬进了课堂。

senses.title: The derivative in calculus
senses.definition: in mathematics, the operation of finding the rate at which a function changes
senses.definitionCN: 数学中求函数变化率的运算
senses.example: Differentiation of that curve gives its slope at every point.
senses.exampleCN: 对那条曲线求微分，就得到它在每一点的斜率。
senses.why: A difference is a gap between two values. Differentiation shrinks that gap toward zero and asks what ratio survives; the word keeps the original 'difference' at its centre.
senses.whyCN: difference 是两个值之间的间隙。微分把这个间隙缩到趋近于零，再看还剩下什么比值；这个词的中心始终是“差”。

senses.title: Magma splitting into rock types
senses.definition: in geology, the process by which a single magma body separates into chemically distinct melts or rocks
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中单一岩浆体分离成化学成分不同的熔体或岩石的过程
senses.example: Magmatic differentiation explains why one volcano erupts several rock types.
senses.exampleCN: 岩浆分异解释了一座火山为何喷出多种岩石。
senses.why: One parent melt is carried apart into several fractions as minerals crystallize out. The geological sense is the laboratory version of 'becoming unlike'.
senses.whyCN: 一个母岩浆随着矿物结晶被“搬成”几个部分。这个地质义就是“变得不同”在实验室里的版本。

senses.title: Society splitting into roles
senses.definition: in sociology, the division of a society into groups and roles with distinct functions
senses.definitionCN: 社会学中社会分成功能不同的群体与角色的过程
senses.example: Urban growth brought sharper social differentiation.
senses.exampleCN: 城市增长带来更明显的社会分化。
senses.why: Modern societies do not do the same work with the same people. Differentiation names the branching of tasks, and with it the branching of identities.
senses.whyCN: 现代社会不再由同一批人做同样的工作。differentiation 命名的是任务的不断分岔，以及随之而来的身份分岔。

senses.title: Parts specializing inside a system
senses.definition: in systems theory and organization, the specialization of parts that once performed a common function
senses.definitionCN: 系统论与组织理论中原本承担共同功能的各部分走向专门化
senses.example: Biological and organizational systems both gain efficiency through differentiation.
senses.exampleCN: 生物系统与组织系统都通过功能分化提高效率。
senses.why: The counterpart of integration: a system splits into specialized parts that must then be coordinated. The word here measures internal specialization, not difference from outsiders.
senses.whyCN: 它是 integration（整合）的对立面：系统分裂成专门化的部分，随后必须被协调。这里的词衡量的是内部分工，而不是与外部者的差异。

intro.en: Differentiation is a Latin verb plus a Latin noun suffix: differre 'to carry apart', its noun differentia 'a difference', the verb differentiate, and finally -ation. English took the verb from French in the 19th century and built the noun on top of it.
intro.cn: differentiation 是拉丁动词加拉丁名词后缀：differre“分开搬运”，其名词 differentia“差异”，动词 differentiate，最后加 -ation。英语在 19 世纪从法语借入动词，再在其上造出名词。

items.en: The root *bher- meant 'to carry'. It supplies Latin ferre and English bear, and it is the second half of differre, 'to carry apart'.
items.cn: 词根 *bher- 意为“携带”。它给出拉丁语 ferre 与英语 bear，也是 differre“分开搬运”的后半部分。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus ferre 'carry' gave differre, 'to carry apart, to differ, to defer'. Its noun differentia named a difference, and the adjective differens named 'different'.
items.cn: dis-“分开”加 ferre“搬运”构成 differre，意为“搬开、相异、推迟”。其名词 differentia 指差异，形容词 differens 指“不同的”。

items.en: The suffix -atio built process nouns from verbs, as in formatio and creatio. Attached to a Latin-derived verb, it yields an English -ation noun naming the process or its result.
items.cn: 后缀 -atio 从动词造出过程名词，如 formatio、creatio。加在拉丁来源的动词上，就得到英语的 -ation 名词，指过程或其结果。

items.en: Old French differencier carried the verb into Middle English as differencien. The noun differentiation appears later, modelled directly on Latin differentia plus -ation.
items.cn: 古法语 differencier 把动词带入中古英语作 differencien。名词 differentiation 出现得更晚，直接仿照拉丁 differentia 加 -ation 构成。

items.en: Calculus gave the word its technical sense: differentiation is the operation inverse to integration. The term spread from French and German textbooks into English in the early 19th century.
items.cn: 微积分赋予这个词技术义：differentiation 是 integration 的逆运算。该术语在 19 世纪初从法语与德语教材传入英语。

items.en: Cell differentiation and social differentiation extend the same image of branching to tissues and to societies. The word now covers both a judgement and a natural process.
items.cn: 细胞分化与社会分化把同一“分岔”意象扩展到组织与社会。这个词现在同时覆盖判断行为与自然过程。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the adjective and the noun that all sit on the same Latin base. The meaning group compares words about difference, separation and specialization.
note.cn: 形近组区分同一拉丁词基上的动词、形容词与名词；词义组比较表示差异、分离与专门化的词。

entries.definition: to tell apart, to make different, or to find a derivative. It is the verb that lies behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 区分、使不同或求导。它是名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: the state of being unlike, or the amount by which two numbers differ. It names the gap, not the process of making one.
entries.definitionCN: 不同的状态，或两数相差的量。它指缝隙本身，而不是制造缝隙的过程。

entries.definition: relating to a difference, or a small amount by which values change. In maths it is the infinitesimal increment.
entries.definitionCN: 与差异有关的，或数值变化的微小量。数学中指无穷小增量。

entries.definition: a difference explicitly recognized or a mark of quality. It stresses the line drawn, while differentiation stresses the process of drawing it.
entries.definitionCN: 被明确认识到的差别，或优异的标志。它强调画出的那条线，而 differentiation 强调画线的过程。

entries.definition: the act of concentrating on one field or function. It is the result of differentiation in biology and in organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 集中于某一领域或功能的行为。它是生物学与组织中分化的结果。

entries.definition: the process of separating and going in different directions. It describes the paths, while differentiation describes the emerging difference.
entries.definitionCN: 分开并朝不同方向发展的过程。它描述路径，而 differentiation 描述显现出的差异。

entries.definition: the ability to see fine differences, or unfair treatment. It is close to sense 01 but carries a social judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 看出细微差别的能力，或指不公平对待。它接近第 1 义项，但带有社会判断。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from differre, 'carry apart', and let the branching image cover cells, products and courses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 differre“分开搬运”搭起这个词，再用分岔意象覆盖细胞、产品与课程。

normal.en: See dis- + ferre: to carry apart. Differentiation is the carrying-apart made into a noun.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 ferre：分开搬运。differentiation 就是“搬开”这个动作变成名词。

normal.en: Picture one stem splitting into two branches: biology calls that cell differentiation.
normal.cn: 想象一根主干分成两枝：生物学把这叫细胞分化。

normal.en: In marketing, the same split happens on a shelf: your product takes its own branch.
normal.cn: 在营销中，同一种分岔发生在货架上：你的产品长出自己的一枝。

normal.en: Connect the maths sense to difference: a derivative measures how fast one value differs from the next.
normal.cn: 把数学义连到 difference：导数衡量一个值相对下一个值变化多快。

normal.en: Remember the pair: differentiation splits, integration joins.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：differentiation 拆开，integration 合拢。

abstract.en: Keep one shape in mind: a single trunk becoming a tree of distinct branches. Every sense is that shape.
abstract.cn: 只记一个形状：一根主干长成一棵分叉的树。每个义项都是这个形状。

abstract.en: Treat the word as a verb of distance: things are carried apart until each has its own name.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作“距离的动词”：东西被搬开，直到每样都有自己的名字。

abstract.en: Notice that the noun never fully loses 'difference': even calculus is still measuring a gap.
abstract.cn: 注意这个名词从未丢掉“difference”：连微积分也仍在测量一个间隙。

examples.en: Careful differentiation between the two hypotheses is essential.
examples.cn: 对这两个假说作出仔细区分至关重要。

examples.en: Cell differentiation turns a single fertilized egg into a whole organism.
examples.cn: 细胞分化把一个受精卵变成完整的生物体。

examples.en: Differentiation of the function gives the velocity at any moment.
examples.cn: 对该函数求微分就得到任意时刻的速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地分人先谢”：大家分地、分开、分家，先分才有 differentiation 的区分与分化。

root: 拉丁语 differre“分开搬运”（dis- 分开 + ferre 携带），名词 differentia“差异”；再经法语 differencier 进入英语作 differentiate，加拉丁名词后缀 -ation 构成 differentiation。数学的“微分”义在 19 世纪从微积分术语中固定下来。

sensesIntro.en: One Latin verb, differre, means 'to carry apart'. Everything in this entry is a version of that carrying: a mind separates two species, a stem cell takes one path, a brand is set apart on a shelf, a magma splits into fractions, a calculus operation shrinks a gap toward zero. The nine senses differ only in what is being separated and who does the separating.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个拉丁动词 differre 意为“分开搬运”。本词条的一切都是这个“搬开”的版本：头脑分辨两个物种，干细胞走上一条路径，品牌在货架上被置开，岩浆分成几部分，微积分运算把间隙缩向零。九个义项的差别只在于分开的是什么、以及由谁来分。

core.en: Carrying apart: making what was one into things that are not interchangeable.
core.cn: 分开搬运：把原本是一体的东西变成不可互换的多件事物。

branches.en: Judgement and process: telling apart, and becoming unlike.
branches.cn: 判断与过程：分辨，以及逐渐变得不同。

branches.en: MATTER: cells taking roles, magma splitting into rock types.
branches.cn: 物质：细胞承担角色，岩浆分成不同岩类。

branches.en: MARKET AND SCHOOL: products set apart, lessons layered.
branches.cn: 市场与学校：产品被置开，课程被分层。

branches.en: CALCULUS: a gap shrunk toward zero.
branches.cn: 微积分：间隙被缩向零。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: societies and organizations dividing into functions.
branches.cn: 系统：社会与组织分成不同功能。

intro.en: Differentiation stacks three elements: dif- (a form of dis-), ferre 'carry', and -ation. The items below show the same base with other suffixes, and show where dis- keeps its 'apart' force.
intro.cn: differentiation 叠了三个成分：dif-（dis- 的一种形式）、ferre“携带”、-ation。下列条目展示同一词基配其他后缀，并展示 dis- 保留“分开”力量的情形。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb and its two nouns. They explain why a word about difference also yields a word about deferring: carrying apart and putting off are the same gesture in time.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词及其两个名词。它们解释了为什么一个关于差异的词同时产生“推迟”义：在时间上把事搬开与推迟，是同一个动作。

items.meaning: the process of distinguishing or specializing
items.example: Differentiation of the two cases took hours.
items.exampleCN: 区分这两个病例花了几个小时。

items.meaning: to distinguish, to make distinct, to find a derivative
items.example: Readers must differentiate fact from opinion.
items.exampleCN: 读者必须把事实与观点区分开。

items.structure: Latin differens, present participle of differre
items.example: The two samples are chemically different.
items.exampleCN: 这两个样本在化学上不同。

items.meaning: the state of being unlike; the amount between two values
items.example: The difference is only a few degrees.

items.meaning: relating to a difference; a small increment
items.meaningCN: 与差异有关的；微小增量
items.example: The differential between the two rates is small.
The accounts differ on one detail.
items.exampleCN: 这些叙述在一个细节上不同。

items.meaning: to put off to a later time
items.example: They deferred the decision until spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们把决定推迟到春天。

items.meaning: to carry back; to point to
items.example: The footnote refers to an earlier study.
items.exampleCN: 脚注指向一项更早的研究。

items.example: The data were transferred to a new drive.
The river made the valley fertile.
items.exampleCN: 这条河使河谷变得肥沃。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry apart; to differ; to defer

definition_zh: 扩散；传播；漫射；（文化）传播；弥漫
definition_en: the spreading of particles, light, ideas or practices from one place or group to another
core_image: 一滴墨落在水中：颜色从浓处向四周慢慢铺开，直到整杯水都变淡蓝
scene: 实验台上，学生把一滴墨滴进一杯清水。On the bench a student drops ink into a glass of water and watches its diffusion from the centre outward.
sceneCN: 这里 diffusion 是「扩散」（第 1、2 个义项：分子扩散与一般传播）；句意：实验台上，学生把墨滴进清水，看它从中心向四周扩散。图中可辨识物件：滴管、玻璃杯、墨水、记录板。

senses.title: Spreading out in all directions
senses.definition: the process by which something spreads widely through a space or a population
senses.definitionCN: 某物在一个空间或人群中广泛铺开的过程
senses.example: The diffusion of the smell filled the whole kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 味道的扩散充满了整个厨房。
senses.why: Latin diffundere is dis- 'apart' plus fundere 'to pour'. Diffusion is a pouring-apart, and the image is liquid finding its own level across a room.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 diffundere 是 dis-“分开”加 fundere“倾倒”。diffusion 就是“倾倒开来”，意象是液体在房间里自己找平。

senses.title: Molecules moving from dense to sparse
senses.definition: in physics and chemistry, the random movement of particles from a region of high concentration to one of low concentration
senses.definitionCN: 物理与化学中粒子从高浓度区域向低浓度区域的随机运动
senses.example: Oxygen reaches the blood by diffusion through the lung wall.
senses.exampleCN: 氧气通过肺壁的扩散进入血液。
senses.why: No pump is needed: particles simply wander, and because there are more of them on one side the net flow points outward. The word names that statistical pouring.
senses.whyCN: 不需要泵：粒子只是随机游走，因为一侧更多，净流动就朝外。这个词命名的就是这种统计意义上的“倾倒”。

senses.title: Ideas travelling between societies
senses.definition: in anthropology, the spread of customs, technologies or beliefs from one culture to another
senses.definitionCN: 人类学中习俗、技术或信仰从一个文化传到另一个文化
senses.example: The diffusion of papermaking moved west along trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 造纸术沿贸易路线向西传播。
senses.why: Cultures are treated as vessels that can be poured into one another. Diffusion stresses spread without conquest, in contrast to imposition by force.
senses.whyCN: 文化被当作可以互相倾倒的容器。diffusion 强调不靠征服的传播，与以武力强加相对。

senses.title: A new product reaching users
senses.definition: in sociology and marketing, the process by which an innovation is adopted by members of a social system over time
senses.definitionCN: 社会学与营销中创新在一段时间内被社会系统成员采纳的过程
senses.example: The diffusion of mobile payment took less than a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 移动支付的扩散用了不到十年。
senses.why: Adoption curves are S-shaped: slow at first, fast in the middle, slow at the end. The word borrows the physics of spreading to describe how a habit fills a population.
senses.whyCN: 采纳曲线呈 S 形：起初慢，中段快，末段又慢。这个词借物理学的铺开来描述一种习惯如何填满人群。

senses.title: Light scattered by a surface
senses.definition: in optics, the scattering of light so that it travels in many directions rather than one beam
senses.definitionCN: 光学中光被散射到多个方向而非保持一束
senses.example: A diffusion sheet softens the harsh studio light.
senses.exampleCN: 柔光片把刺眼的摄影灯变柔。
senses.why: A beam poured apart loses its direction. The optical sense keeps the original image literally: light is the liquid that spreads.
senses.whyCN: 一束光被“倾倒开”就失去方向。这个光学义把原意象照字面保留：光就是被铺开的液体。

senses.title: A species or disease spreading
senses.definition: in geography and epidemiology, the spread of organisms or infections across space
senses.definitionCN: 地理学与流行病学中生物或传染病在空间上的扩散
senses.example: The diffusion of the virus followed air routes.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒的扩散沿着航线展开。
senses.why: Here the spread has carriers and a map. Diffusion still means pouring outward, but the medium is now a population of hosts or habitats.
senses.whyCN: 这里的扩散有携带者、有地图。diffusion 仍指向外倾倒，但介质变成了宿主或栖息地的人群。

senses.title: A language feature crossing borders
senses.definition: in linguistics, the spread of a sound, word or construction from one language or region into another
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中语音、词或结构从一个语言或地区传入另一个
senses.example: The diffusion of the suffix across dialects took centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个后缀在各方言间的扩散花了数百年。
senses.why: Languages are in contact, and forms seep across the boundary. The word is chosen when the emphasis is on gradual seepage rather than borrowing by a single act.
senses.whyCN: 语言相互接触，形式从边界渗过去。当强调的是缓慢渗透而非一次性借用时，就用这个词。

senses.title: Heat spreading through a material
senses.definition: in physics, the transfer of heat through a substance by conduction at the molecular level
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中热在物质内通过分子层面的传导而传递
senses.example: Thermal diffusion keeps the metal plate evenly warm.
senses.exampleCN: 热扩散使金属板保持均匀温热。
senses.why: Heat is not a thing that is pushed; it is molecular motion handed along. The same pour-image is applied to energy instead of matter.
senses.whyCN: 热不是被推着走的物体，而是被逐层传递的分子运动。同一个“倾倒”意象被用在能量而非物质上。

senses.title: Power distributed among actors
senses.definition: in political science, the dispersion of authority among many institutions or actors
senses.definitionCN: 政治学中权威分散到许多机构或行为者之间
senses.example: The diffusion of power made negotiation slower but steadier.
senses.exampleCN: 权力的分散使谈判更慢，但更稳。
senses.why: When authority is poured out among many hands, no single centre can decide alone. The metaphor shifts from substance to influence.
senses.whyCN: 当权威被倾倒到许多只手里，就没有单一中心能独自决定。这个比喻从物质转向了影响力。

intro.en: Diffusion is Latin diffundere plus -io. The verb joins dis- 'apart' to fundere 'to pour', so the core meaning is 'a pouring apart'. English took the noun from French and Latin in the 14th century.
intro.cn: diffusion 是拉丁 diffundere 加 -io。动词把 dis-“分开”与 fundere“倾倒”结合，核心义即“倾倒开来”。英语在 14 世纪从法语与拉丁语借入这个名词。

items.en: The root *gheu- meant 'to pour'. Latin fundere comes from it, and so do English gut and the geological term geyser through other branches.
items.cn: 词根 *gheu- 意为“倾倒”。拉丁语 fundere 由此而来，英语 gut 与地质术语 geyser 也经其他分支同出此源。

items.en: Fundere meant 'to pour out, to shed'. With dis- it became diffundere, 'to pour in different directions, to spread'. Its participle diffusus gave the adjective diffuse.
items.cn: fundere 意为“倒出、流洒”。加 dis- 成为 diffundere“向不同方向倾倒、铺开”。其分词 diffusus 给出形容词 diffuse。

items.en: The noun diffusio named a spreading out. Latin used it for scattering in general, not yet for molecules or ideas.
items.cn: 名词 diffusio 指铺开、散布。拉丁语用它泛指散射，尚未用于分子或观念。

items.en: French diffusion and Latin diffusio entered English in the 14th century with the general sense of spreading. The optical sense appears early, since light was the classic thing that spreads.
items.cn: 法语 diffusion 与拉丁 diffusio 在 14 世纪进入英语，带一般“铺开”义。光学义出现得早，因为光正是经典会铺开的东西。

items.en: With the kinetic theory of matter, diffusion became a precise term for particles moving down a concentration gradient. Fick's law of 1855 fixed the mathematical form.
items.cn: 随着物质运动论，diffusion 成为粒子沿浓度梯度运动的精确术语。1855 年的菲克定律固定了其数学形式。

items.en: Anthropology and sociology borrowed the physical term for the spread of culture and innovations. The metaphor was explicit: ideas were said to flow through a social medium.
items.cn: 人类学与社会学借用物理术语，指文化与创新的传播。这个比喻是明说的：观念被描述为在社会介质中流动。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the adjective and the equipment noun. The meaning group contrasts spreading with pouring in, mixing and forcing.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、形容词与器具名词；词义组对比“铺开”与“倒入”“混合”“强加”。

entries.definition: to spread out, or spread out and lacking focus. The verb is stressed on the second syllable; the adjective has the same spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 扩散；散漫的、不集中的。动词重音在第二音节，形容词拼写相同。

entries.definition: a device that spreads light, air or scent. It is the instrument, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 使光、空气或香气散开的装置。它指器具，不是过程。

entries.definition: tending to spread out. It describes the tendency, while diffusion names the process.
entries.definitionCN: 有散布倾向的。它描述倾向，而 diffusion 指过程。

entries.definition: the act of pouring something in, as tea steeping or a quality being introduced. Same fundere, opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物倒入，如泡茶或注入某种品质。同出 fundere，方向相反。

entries.definition: the act of extending over a wider area. It is the plain English word that diffusion translates in technical contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 扩展到更大范围的行为。它是 diffusion 在技术语境中的普通英语对应词。

entries.definition: the scattering of particles or a population. It stresses separation into scattered units, while diffusion stresses net flow.
entries.definitionCN: 粒子或人群的散开。它强调散成各单位，而 diffusion 强调净流动。

entries.definition: the movement of a solvent through a membrane into a more concentrated solution. A special case of diffusion.
entries.definitionCN: 溶剂穿膜进入浓度更高溶液的运动。它是扩散的特例。

entries.definition: the act of sending something along, as a signal or a disease. It implies a chain of givers and receivers rather than a medium filling.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物传下去，如信号或疾病。它暗示传递者与接受者的链条，而非介质被填满。

normalIntro.en: These hooks anchor the word in the single image of pouring apart, then move that image through physics, culture and optics.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩先把词钉在“倾倒开来”这一个意象上，再把意象依次挪到物理、文化与光学。

normal.en: Split the word: dif- = apart, -fus- = pour. Diffusion is a pouring apart.
normal.cn: 拆词：dif- 表示分开，-fus- 表示倾倒。diffusion 就是“倒开”。

normal.en: Picture ink in water: no stirring, just net flow from dark to pale.
normal.cn: 想象墨在水里：不搅拌，只是从浓处向淡处的净流动。

normal.en: Contrast infusion: in-pouring makes tea; diffusion is the same pour without a boundary.
normal.cn: 对比 infusion：往里倒才泡出茶；diffusion 是同样的倒，但没有边界。

normal.en: For culture, think of papermaking travelling west along trade routes, not by armies.
normal.cn: 文化方面，想造纸术沿着贸易路线西传，而不是靠军队。

normal.en: For optics, a diffusion sheet turns one beam into a soft glow.
normal.cn: 光学方面，柔光片把一束光变成柔和的光晕。

abstract.en: Reduce the whole entry to one sentence: anything concentrated will drift toward where it is scarce.
abstract.cn: 把整条词条缩成一句：任何浓的东西都会漂向它稀薄的地方。

abstract.en: Notice that the word needs no agent. Diffusion happens; nobody is pouring.
abstract.cn: 注意这个词不需要施动者。扩散自己发生；没有人在倒。

abstract.en: Use the same question for every sense: what is the medium, and what is spreading through it?
abstract.cn: 每个义项都问同一个问题：介质是什么，又是什么在介质中铺开？

examples.en: The diffusion of English loanwords into Japanese accelerated in the twentieth century.
examples.cn: 英语借词向日语的扩散在二十世纪加快。

examples.en: Diffusion is faster in a gas than in a solid.
examples.cn: 扩散在气体中比在固体中快。

examples.en: The report traces the diffusion of the technology across three continents.
examples.cn: 该报告追踪这项技术跨三大洲的扩散。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地浮云”：雾气从地面浮起、像云一样铺满天空，就是 diffusion 的扩散。

root: 拉丁语 diffundere“向不同方向倾倒、铺开”（dis- 分开 + fundere 倾倒），名词 diffusio；经法语 diffusion 于 14 世纪进入英语。同族 fundere 还给出 infusion（倒入）、confusion（混在一起）、refund（倒回）。

sensesIntro.en: Diffusion names one physical gesture, pouring apart, and then applies it to whatever can spread: molecules, light, heat, customs, innovations, languages, viruses, even authority. The senses differ in medium and in whether the spread is literal or metaphorical, but none of them loses the original image of something concentrated becoming evenly distributed.
sensesIntro.cn: diffusion 命名一个物理动作——倾倒开来，然后把它用到任何能铺开的东西上：分子、光、热、习俗、创新、语言、病毒，甚至权力。各义项在介质上不同，在“实指还是比喻”上不同，但没有一个丢掉原意象：浓的东西变得均匀分布。

core.en: A pouring apart: what is concentrated spreads until it fills the space around it.
core.cn: 倾倒开来：浓的东西铺开，直到填满周围空间。

branches.en: PHYSICS: smell, molecules and heat finding their own level.
branches.cn: 物理：气味、分子与热各自找平。

branches.en: CULTURE: customs and innovations spreading through a society.
branches.cn: 文化：习俗与创新在社会中铺开。

branches.en: OPTICS: a beam poured apart into many directions.
branches.cn: 光学：一束光被倒散成许多方向。

branches.en: LIFE AND LANGUAGE: species, infections and forms crossing borders.
branches.cn: 生命与语言：物种、传染病与语言形式越过边界。

branches.en: POLITICS: authority dispersed among many hands.
branches.cn: 政治：权威分散到许多只手里。

intro.en: Diffusion is dis- plus the fundere family plus -io. The items show how the same 'pour' root keeps turning up in words that look unrelated: refund, confuse, futile.
intro.cn: diffusion 是 dis- 加 fundere 词族再加 -io。下列条目展示同一个“倾倒”词根如何出现在看似无关的词里：refund、confuse、futile。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are the verb, its participle and the noun. They show that 'confused' and 'diffused' are cousins: one pours things together, the other pours them apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目是动词、分词与名词。它们说明 confused 与 diffused 是表亲：一个把东西倒在一起，一个把它们倒开。

items.example: Diffusion carried the scent across the room.
items.exampleCN: 扩散把气味带过整个房间。

items.example: The lamp diffuses light evenly.

items.meaning: a device that spreads light, air or scent
items.meaningCN: 使光、空气或香气散开的装置
items.example: The diffuser softened the stage lighting.
items.exampleCN: 柔光罩把舞台灯光变柔。

items.example: The material has diffusive properties.

items.meaning: a pouring in; an added quality
items.example: An infusion of new funds saved the project.
items.exampleCN: 新资金的注入救了该项目。

items.meaning: a pouring together; disorder of mind
items.example: The two names cause constant confusion.
items.exampleCN: 这两个名字不断引起混淆。

items.meaning: to pour back; to give money back
items.example: The shop refunded the full price.

items.meaning: a pouring across, as of blood
items.example: The patient needed a blood transfusion.
Further argument seemed futile.

latinEntries.meaning: to pour, to shed, to scatter
to pour in different directions; to spread

definition_zh: 尺寸的；量纲的；……维的；立体的；有深度的
definition_en: relating to measurements or dimensions, or having a stated number of dimensions
core_image: 一把游标卡尺同时量出长、宽、高：三个方向都标上刻度
scene: 车间工作台上，工人用卡尺测量一个金属块的长、宽、高。At the workbench the worker measures the length, width and height of a metal block and marks the three dimensional measurements on the drawing.
sceneCN: 这里 dimensional 是「尺寸的；三维的」（第 1、2、4 个义项：空间维度与测量）；句意：工人用卡尺量出金属块的长、宽、高，并把三个尺寸标在图纸上。图中可辨识物件：卡尺、金属块、标注长宽高的图纸。

pos.zh: 尺寸的；量纲的；……维的；立体的

derivatives.zh: 维度；尺寸；方面；标注尺寸

senses.title: Relating to length, width and height
senses.definition: of or relating to the measurements that define the size of an object in space
senses.definitionCN: 与界定物体空间大小的测量有关的
senses.example: The dimensional tolerances are given in millimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 尺寸公差以毫米给出。
senses.why: Latin dimetiri is dis- 'apart' plus metiri 'to measure'. A dimension is a measuring-apart, and dimensional means 'belonging to that measuring'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dimetiri 是 dis-“分开”加 metiri“测量”。维度就是“分开地量”，dimensional 意为“属于这种测量的”。

senses.title: Having a stated number of dimensions
senses.definition: used after a number to say how many independent directions a space or figure has
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字后，表示一个空间或图形有几个独立方向
senses.example: The model is a three-dimensional grid of points.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型是一个三维点阵。
senses.why: A point needs one number to locate, a plane needs two, a solid needs three. Adding a dimension means adding one more independent measurement.
senses.whyCN: 定位一个点需要一个数，一个平面需要两个，一个立体需要三个。增加一维就是增加一个独立的测量。

senses.title: Measured in size and shape
senses.definition: describing the accuracy or constancy of the physical size of a manufactured part
senses.definitionCN: 描述制造零件物理尺寸的精确程度或稳定程度
senses.example: Wood is less dimensionally stable than steel.
senses.exampleCN: 木材的尺寸稳定性不如钢。
senses.why: In manufacturing the question is not how many directions but how faithfully the measured size matches the drawing. Dimensional becomes a quality label.
senses.whyCN: 在制造中，问题不是有几个方向，而是实测尺寸多忠实地符合图纸。dimensional 于是成了一个质量标签。

senses.title: Looking solid rather than flat
senses.definition: appearing to have depth as well as height and width, as an image or a film
senses.definitionCN: 像图像或影片那样显得除了高宽之外还有深度
senses.example: The new screen gives a dimensional feel to the drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 新屏幕让这张图有了立体感。
senses.why: The eye reads shading and perspective as extra measurements. A flat picture that supplies them is called dimensional because it restores the third axis.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛把明暗与透视读成额外的测量。一幅提供了这些的平面图像被称为立体的，因为它恢复了第三根轴。

senses.title: Having depth of character
senses.definition: figuratively, having complexity and depth rather than being simple or flat
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义上具有复杂性与深度，而非单薄扁平
senses.example: The novel offers a dimensional portrait of its villain.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说给反派画了一幅有层次的肖像。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the solid object: a flat character has one surface, a dimensional one can be walked around. Depth becomes moral and psychological.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了立体物：扁平角色只有一个面，有维度的角色可以绕着走。深度于是变成道德与心理上的东西。

senses.title: A single aspect of a problem
senses.titleCN: 某一方面的（常与数词连用）
senses.definition: in combinations such as one-dimensional, referring to a single aspect or view of a complex matter
senses.definitionCN: 在 one-dimensional 等组合中，指复杂事情的单一侧面或视角
senses.example: The debate was one-dimensional, ignoring costs entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论只有一个维度，完全忽略了成本。
senses.why: A one-dimensional account has only one axis along which to vary. The word turns a geometric count into a criticism of narrowness.
senses.whyCN: 单一维度的叙述只有一根可以变化的轴。这个词把几何上的计数变成了对狭隘的批评。

senses.title: Checking units by their dimensions
senses.definition: in science, relating to the method of checking equations by comparing the physical dimensions of their terms
senses.definitionCN: 科学中通过比较各项物理量纲来检验方程的方法
senses.example: Dimensional analysis shows the formula must be wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 量纲分析表明这个公式一定有错。
senses.why: Metiri gave the word 'measure'; a dimension is a kind of measure, such as length or time. Dimensional analysis asks whether both sides of an equation measure the same kind of thing.
senses.whyCN: metiri 给出“测量”；量纲是一种测量类别，如长度或时间。量纲分析追问方程两边量的是不是同一类东西。

senses.title: Keeping the same size over time
senses.definition: remaining unchanged in physical size under changes of temperature, moisture or load
senses.definitionCN: 在温度、湿度或载荷变化下物理尺寸保持不变
senses.example: The composite is dimensionally stable under heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这种复合材料受热时尺寸稳定。
senses.why: Here dimension means the measured size itself. A material that does not grow or shrink has kept its measurements, so it is dimensionally stable.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 dimension 指被量出的尺寸本身。不胀不缩的材料守住了它的测量值，所以是尺寸稳定的。

intro.en: Dimensional is dimension plus -al. Dimension comes from Latin dimensio, a noun from dimetiri 'to measure out', built on metiri 'to measure'. The adjective is a later English formation, and its technical senses grew in mathematics, engineering and criticism.
intro.cn: dimensional 是 dimension 加 -al。dimension 来自拉丁 dimensio，由 dimetiri“量出”而来，其词根是 metiri“测量”。形容词是较晚的英语构造，其技术义在数学、工程与文艺批评中各自生长。

items.en: The root *me- meant 'to measure'. It gives Latin metiri, English meal in the old sense of 'measured portion', and the Greek metron behind metre and symmetry.
items.cn: 词根 *me- 意为“测量”。它给出拉丁 metiri、英语 meal（古义“一份量”），以及 metre 与 symmetry 背后的希腊 metron。

items.en: Metiri meant 'to measure'. With dis- it became dimetiri, 'to measure out, to mark off', used by Roman land surveyors laying out plots.
items.cn: metiri 意为“测量”。加 dis- 成为 dimetiri“量出、划出”，罗马土地测量员用它来划分地块。

items.en: The noun dimensio named a measuring-out and then the measure itself. Latin used it for the size of a body and for the parts of a geometric figure.
items.cn: 名词 dimensio 指量出的动作，后指量出的结果。拉丁语用它指物体的大小与几何图形的各部分。

items.en: English dimension arrives in the 16th century from French, first as 'measurement, size'. The geometric sense of an axis of space is fixed in the 17th century.
items.cn: 英语 dimension 于 16 世纪从法语进入，初义为“测量、大小”。空间轴线的几何义在 17 世纪固定。

items.en: The adjective dimensional appears in the 18th century, and compounds such as three-dimensional spread with geometry teaching and later with printing and film.
items.cn: 形容词 dimensional 出现于 18 世纪，three-dimensional 等复合词随几何教学传播，后又随印刷与电影扩散。

items.en: Dimensional analysis enters physics in the 19th century; dimensional stability enters engineering; the figurative 'flat or full character' use enters criticism in the 20th.
items.cn: 量纲分析在 19 世纪进入物理学；尺寸稳定性进入工程学；比喻性的“扁平或有层次的角色”用法在 20 世纪进入文艺批评。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun, its negation and the adverb. The meaning group contrasts dimensions with mere size, with spatial extent and with measurement generally.
note.cn: 形近组区分名词、其否定形式与副词；词义组把“维度”与单纯的“大小”“空间范围”“一般测量”区分开。

entries.definition: a measurement in space, an aspect of a situation, or a level of a problem. The adjective is built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 空间中的测量、情境的一面，或问题的一个层面。形容词由它构成。

entries.definition: having no physical units, as a pure ratio. It is the opposite technical pole from dimensional.
entries.definitionCN: 没有物理单位的，如纯比值。它是在技术义上与 dimensional 相反的一端。

entries.definition: in terms of dimensions or measurements. The adverb modifies a verb; the adjective modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 就维度或尺寸而言。副词修饰动词，形容词修饰名词。

entries.definition: relating to space and the position of things in it. It names the field, while dimensional names the measurements within it.
entries.definitionCN: 与空间及事物在其中的位置有关的。它指领域，而 dimensional 指领域内的度量。

entries.definition: relating to the properties of shapes. A geometric figure has dimensionality, but a dimensional report also includes tolerances.
entries.definitionCN: 与图形性质有关的。几何图形有维度，而尺寸报告还包含公差。

entries.definition: relating to measurement by volume. It specifies what is measured, whereas dimensional only says that measuring is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 与按体积测量有关的。它指明量的是什么，而 dimensional 只说涉及测量。

entries.definition: capable of being measured. A dimensional claim presupposes that something measurable exists.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被测量的。尺寸方面的论断预设了有可测之物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from the measuring root met-, then attach the three counts that matter: length, width, height.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从测量词根 met- 搭起这个词，再挂上真正重要的三个数：长、宽、高。

normal.en: See di- + metiri: measuring apart, one axis at a time.
normal.cn: 看见 di- 加 metiri：一根轴一根轴地分开量。

normal.en: Count the numbers needed to locate a point: one, two, three. That count is the dimension.
normal.cn: 数一数定位一个点需要几个数：一个、两个、三个。这个数目就是维数。

normal.en: In a workshop, dimensional means the part matches the drawing in size.
normal.cn: 在车间里，dimensional 指零件的尺寸符合图纸。

normal.en: Link three-dimensional with film: the screen adds a third axis to a flat picture.
normal.cn: 把 three-dimensional 连到电影：屏幕给平面图像加上了第三根轴。

normal.en: Remember one-dimensional as an insult: only one axis, so no breadth of view.
normal.cn: 记住 one-dimensional 是贬义：只有一根轴，因而没有视野的宽度。

abstract.en: Hold the image of a caliper closing on a block: every sense of the word comes from that closing.
abstract.cn: 抓住卡尺夹住金属块的意象：这个词的每个义项都来自那一次夹合。

abstract.en: Treat dimensions as questions you can ask of a thing: how long, how wide, how deep, how complex.
abstract.cn: 把维度当作可以问一件事的问题：多长、多宽、多深、多复杂。

abstract.en: Notice that a dimension is not a thing but a way of measuring; the adjective always implies a frame.
abstract.cn: 注意维度不是东西，而是测量的方式；这个形容词总是隐含着一个参照框架。

examples.en: The painter achieves a dimensional effect with light and shadow alone.
examples.cn: 这位画家仅凭光影就取得了立体效果。

examples.en: Dimensional analysis caught the error before the experiment began.
examples.cn: 量纲分析在实验开始前就抓到了错误。

examples.en: The alloy stays dimensionally stable at high temperatures.
examples.cn: 这种合金在高温下尺寸保持稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地门神哪儿”：量地、量门、量神龛，哪儿都要量尺寸——dimensional 就是尺寸与维度的。

root: 拉丁语 metiri“测量”，加 dis- 成 dimetiri“量出、划出”，名词 dimensio“量出的结果、大小”；经法语进入英语作 dimension，再加形容词后缀 -al 构成 dimensional。同根词有 metre、measure、symmetry（希腊同源 metron）。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of dimensional comes from one act: measuring out. The word asks how many independent measurements a thing needs, or how faithfully its measured size holds. From that single question it reaches geometry, engineering tolerance, the illusion of depth on a flat screen, and finally the metaphor of a character or argument that has more than one side.
sensesIntro.cn: dimensional 的每个义项都来自同一个动作：量出。这个词追问一件事需要几个独立的测量，或它被量出的尺寸有多可靠。从这一个问题出发，它伸到几何、工程公差、平面屏幕上的深度错觉，最后到“角色或论点不止一面”的比喻。

core.en: Measured out: assigning numbers along independent axes.
core.cn: 量出：沿着彼此独立的轴赋予数值。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: size, tolerance and stability of a real object.
branches.cn: 测量：真实物体的尺寸、公差与稳定性。

branches.en: GEOMETRY AND PHYSICS: how many axes, and whether units balance.
branches.cn: 几何与物理：有几根轴，以及单位是否配平。

branches.en: ILLUSION: a flat image restored to three axes.
branches.cn: 错觉：平面图像被恢复成三根轴。

branches.en: CHARACTER: a person or work that can be walked around.
branches.cn: 性格：可以绕着看的人或作品。

branches.en: NARROW VIEW: a complex matter reduced to one aspect.
branches.cn: 狭窄视角：复杂之事被缩到一面。

intro.en: Dimensional is a noun plus -al, and the noun itself is a prefixed form of the measuring root. The items trace that root through English and show the negative and abstract forms built on dimension.
intro.cn: dimensional 是名词加 -al，名词本身又是测量词根加前缀的形式。下列条目追踪这个词根在英语中的走向，并展示由 dimension 构成的否定与抽象形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb of measuring and its two derived nouns. They explain why 'dimension' can mean both a line on a drawing and a facet of a story.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出测量的动词及其两个派生名词。它们解释了为什么 dimension 既能指图纸上的一条标注，也能指故事的一个侧面。

items.example: The dimensional error was under a tenth of a millimetre.
items.exampleCN: 尺寸误差不到十分之一毫米。

items.example: Cost is only one dimension of the problem.
items.exampleCN: 成本只是这个问题的一个方面。

items.example: Reynolds number is dimensionless.

items.meaning: the number or quality of dimensions
items.example: The dataset has high dimensionality.
The two parts are dimensionally identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两个零件在尺寸上完全相同。

items.meaning: to determine size; a size determined
items.example: Measure the board before cutting.

items.meaning: a unit of length; poetic measure
items.example: The room is four metres long.

items.meaning: the same measure on both sides; balance
items.example: The building's symmetry pleases the eye.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑的对称令人悦目。

items.example: The immense plain stretched to the horizon.
items.exampleCN: 巨大的平原一直延伸到地平线。

latinEntries.meaning: to measure out, to mark off

definition_zh: 不利条件；缺点；劣势；损害；使处于不利地位
definition_en: a condition that makes someone or something less likely to succeed, or the act of putting them in such a condition
core_image: 赛跑时一个人被要求晚一步起跑：起跑线在他身后半米
scene: 操场上，一个学生站在比其他人都靠后的起跑线上，教练指着那条退后的白线说：that is a clear disadvantage。
sceneCN: 这里 disadvantage 是「不利条件、劣势」（第 1、2 个义项：不利处境）；句意：那条退后的起跑线就是一种明显的不利。图中可辨识物件：跑道、退后的白色起跑线、秒表、其他选手。

pos.zh: 不利条件；缺点；劣势；损害

senses.title: A condition that works against you
senses.definition: a circumstance that reduces the chance of success or makes progress harder
senses.definitionCN: 降低成功机会或使进展更困难的境况
senses.example: Poor transport is a serious disadvantage for rural students.
senses.exampleCN: 交通不便对农村学生是严重的不利条件。
senses.why: Dis- here is privative: it removes an advantage rather than splitting something apart. The word is advantage with its favourable force deleted.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 dis- 是“否定”前缀：它撤走一项优势，而不是把东西分开。这个词就是被删掉了有利之力的 advantage。

senses.title: A drawback of a plan
senses.definition: a feature of a proposal or object that counts against it
senses.definitionCN: 使某个提议或物品减分的特点
senses.example: The main disadvantage of the design is its weight.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计的主要缺点是重量。
senses.why: When weighing options, each feature is placed on one side of a balance. A disadvantage is the weight that pulls the scale down.
senses.whyCN: 权衡方案时，每个特点都被放到天平的一端。disadvantage 就是把秤盘压下去的那块重量。

senses.title: Social and economic deprivation
senses.definition: the condition of lacking resources, opportunities or access that others have
senses.definitionCN: 缺少他人拥有的资源、机会或准入资格的状态
senses.example: The programme targets areas of long-term disadvantage.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目针对长期处于弱势的地区。
senses.why: Here the missing advantage is not a single feature but a whole set of resources. The pluralised social use turns the word into a label for inequality.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺的不是某一项特点，而是一整套资源。社会语境中的用法把这个词变成了不平等的标签。

senses.title: Being in a weaker position
senses.definition: the state of being placed in circumstances that favour others over you, especially in the phrase at a disadvantage
senses.definitionCN: 处于对他人更有利的处境，尤用于短语 at a disadvantage
senses.example: Without the data, we are negotiating at a disadvantage.
senses.exampleCN: 没有这些数据，我们谈判时处于不利地位。
senses.why: The phrase locates a person at a point on a slope, lower than the other party. It is positional, not a list of flaws.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把人放在斜坡上的一个点，比对方更低。它是位置性的，而不是一串缺点清单。

senses.title: A handicap conceded in a contest
senses.titleCN: 竞赛中让出的不利条件
senses.definition: in sport or games, a handicap or starting disadvantage imposed to equalize chances
senses.definitionCN: 体育或竞赛中为使机会均等而施加的让步或起跑劣势
senses.example: The faster runner started with a time disadvantage.
senses.exampleCN: 较快的跑者带着时间上的劣势起跑。
senses.why: A handicap is literally a hand in cap, an old drawing device. The disadvantage is imposed on the stronger side to make the contest fair, which inverts the usual sense.
senses.whyCN: handicap 字面是“帽子里的手”，一种古老的抽签装置。这种劣势被施加在较强的一方以求公平，正好颠倒了通常的含义。

senses.title: Losing ground to rivals
senses.definition: in business, a factor that leaves a firm weaker than its competitors in cost, access or reputation
senses.definitionCN: 商业中使公司在成本、渠道或声誉上弱于对手的因素
senses.example: Higher energy costs put local mills at a competitive disadvantage.
senses.exampleCN: 更高的能源成本使本地工厂处于竞争劣势。
senses.why: The balance image returns at market scale: one firm carries a cost others do not. The word measures relative position, not absolute failure.
senses.whyCN: 天平意象回到市场尺度：一家公司背着别人没有的成本。这个词衡量的是相对位置，而非绝对失败。

senses.title: Gaps in schooling
senses.definition: in education, the lack of prior knowledge, support or opportunity that slows a learner
senses.definitionCN: 教育中缺少先备知识、支持或机会，从而拖慢学习者
senses.example: Early reading difficulty becomes an educational disadvantage.
senses.exampleCN: 早期阅读困难会变成教育上的劣势。
senses.why: The word is applied to a starting point rather than a verdict. What is missing at the start keeps compounding unless something intervenes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被用在起点，而不是判决。起点缺的东西会不断累积，除非有干预。

senses.title: Acting to someone's harm
senses.definition: as a verb, to place someone in a worse position or to act against their interest
senses.definitionCN: 作动词时，使某人处于更差的处境，或做出违背其利益的事
senses.example: The rule disadvantages small suppliers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项规则使小供应商处于不利地位。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb keeps its privative force: to disadvantage is to strip an advantage from someone. English readily converts nouns of condition into verbs of causing that condition.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词后保留否定力量：to disadvantage 就是从某人身上撤走优势。英语很自然地把状态名词转成“造成该状态”的动词。

senses.title: A point against an argument
senses.definition: in discussion, a consideration that tells against a proposal or theory
senses.definitionCN: 讨论中不利于某个提议或理论的考量
senses.example: The strongest disadvantage of the theory is its cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论最不利的一点是成本。
senses.why: Debate keeps a ledger: each point is entered on the pro or con side. The disadvantage is an entry on the con side, not a personal lack.
senses.whyCN: 辩论有一本账：每个要点都被记在赞成或反对一侧。disadvantage 是记在反对栏的一条，而不是个人的缺失。

intro.en: Disadvantage is advantage with the privative prefix dis-. Advantage comes from Old French avantage, from avant 'before', from Latin ab ante. The word therefore begins as 'being in front', and the prefix reverses that position.
intro.cn: disadvantage 是 advantage 加否定前缀 dis-。advantage 来自古法语 avantage，源于 avant“在前”，再上溯拉丁 ab ante。因此这个词本义是“处在前面”，前缀把这个位置反转过来。

items.en: Ab ante meant 'from before'. The two words fused into a prepositional phrase of place and time, and French avant came from it, meaning 'before, in front'.
items.cn: ab ante 意为“从前面”。两个词融合成一个表地点与时间的短语，法语 avant 由此而来，意为“在前、在面前”。

items.en: Old French avantage named a position in front, and from there a superior position in battle or bargaining. The modern sense of benefit is already present.
items.cn: 古法语 avantage 指“在前的位置”，由此引申为战斗或议价中的优越地位。现代的“利益”义已经出现。

items.en: English advantage appears in the 14th century as 'favourable position'. The phrase at advantage and later at an advantage keeps the spatial metaphor visible.
items.cn: 英语 advantage 于 14 世纪出现，意为“有利位置”。短语 at advantage 及后来的 at an advantage 让空间比喻一直可见。

items.en: The privative dis- was added to form disadvantage, 'a position that is not in front'. The prefix here negates rather than separates, unlike its use in diffusion or differentiation.
items.cn: 否定性的 dis- 被加上，构成 disadvantage“不在前面的位置”。这里的 dis- 是否定而非分开，与它在 diffusion 或 differentiation 中的用法不同。

items.en: The word widens from personal position to the drawbacks of goods and plans, and by the 19th century to social conditions that hold groups back.
items.cn: 这个词从个人位置扩展到商品与方案的缺点，到 19 世纪又扩展到拖住某些群体的社会状况。

items.en: The verb use, 'to put at a disadvantage', becomes common in policy and legal writing in the 20th century, alongside the adjective disadvantaged.
items.cn: 动词用法“使处于不利地位”在 20 世纪的政策与法律写作中变得常见，形容词 disadvantaged 同时通行。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the base noun, its adjective and the antonym. The meaning group contrasts a structural handicap with simple flaws and costs.
note.cn: 形近组区分基础名词、其形容词与反义词；词义组把结构性的劣势与单纯的缺点、代价区分开。

entries.definition: a favourable condition or position. Remove the privative prefix and the scale tips the other way.
entries.definitionCN: 有利条件或位置。去掉否定前缀，天平就倒向另一边。

entries.definition: placed in a worse position, especially by social or economic conditions. It describes the person, not the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 被置于更差处境的，尤因社会或经济条件。它描述人，而不是条件本身。

entries.definition: causing or constituting a disadvantage. It describes the effect of a thing rather than a person's state.
entries.definitionCN: 造成不利的，或构成不利的。它描述事物的效果，而非人的状态。

entries.definition: a disadvantage of a product or plan. It is close to sense 02 but is used almost only of things, not people.
entries.definitionCN: 产品或计划的缺点。它接近第 2 义项，但几乎只用于事物，不用于人。

entries.definition: a condition that makes progress harder, or an advantage conceded in sport. It stresses an imposed or physical burden.
entries.definitionCN: 使进展更困难的条件，或体育中让出的优势。它强调被施加的或身体上的负担。

entries.definition: the negative aspect of something otherwise good. It is conversational and pairs with upside.
entries.definitionCN: 原本不错之事的负面一面。它偏口语，与 upside 配对。

entries.definition: something that blocks progress. It is an external barrier, while a disadvantage is a weaker starting position.
entries.definitionCN: 阻碍进展的东西。它是外部障碍，而 disadvantage 是更弱的起点。

entries.definition: a legal obligation, or a person or thing that holds one back. The business sense is close to competitive disadvantage.
entries.definitionCN: 法律义务，或拖累人的事物。其商业义接近竞争劣势。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word tied to a starting line, then show how the same missing advantage becomes a flaw, a social label and a verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词钉在起跑线上，再展示同一份“缺失的优势”如何变成缺点、社会标签与动词。

normal.en: Read the word as dis- + advantage: an advantage removed, not a thing split.
normal.cn: 把词读作 dis- 加 advantage：一份被撤走的优势，而不是被分开的东西。

normal.en: Picture the runner half a metre behind the line. That metre is the disadvantage.
normal.cn: 想象跑者落后起跑线半米。那半米就是 disadvantage。

normal.en: Keep the balance image: each drawback is a weight on the wrong pan.
normal.cn: 记住天平意象：每个缺点都是压在错误一侧秤盘的重量。

normal.en: Note the fixed phrase at a disadvantage: it is about position, not a list of faults.
normal.cn: 注意固定短语 at a disadvantage：它说的是位置，不是缺点清单。

normal.en: Remember the verb: to disadvantage someone is to take their head start away.
normal.cn: 记住动词：to disadvantage 某人就是拿走他的领先起跑。

abstract.en: Reduce all senses to one question: compared with whom, and starting how far behind?
abstract.cn: 把所有义项缩成一个问题：跟谁比，起跑时落后多少？

abstract.en: Notice the prefix switch: dis- here deletes, while in diffusion it separates. Same shape, different job.
abstract.cn: 注意前缀的切换：这里的 dis- 是删除，而在 diffusion 中是分开。形状相同，工作不同。

abstract.en: Treat the word as relational: nobody is disadvantaged alone, only against a standard or a rival.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作关系性的：没有人独自处于劣势，只在相对某个标准或对手时才是。

examples.en: The report lists the advantages and disadvantages of each option.
examples.cn: 报告列出了每个选项的利弊。

examples.en: Children from poorer neighbourhoods face an educational disadvantage from the start.
examples.cn: 较贫困社区的孩子从一开始就面临教育劣势。

examples.en: Any delay would disadvantage the smaller suppliers.
examples.cn: 任何拖延都会使较小的供应商处于不利地位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地塞得万天机”：地把万千天机都塞住了，你自然就落了下风——disadvantage 就是劣势。

root: advantage 来自古法语 avantage，源于 avant“在前”，再上溯拉丁 ab ante“从前面”；加否定前缀 dis- 构成 disadvantage，表示“不在前面的位置”，即不利条件。这里的 dis- 是否定性的，与表示“分开”的 dis- 不同源义。

sensesIntro.en: Disadvantage is a positional word before it is a moral one. It begins with the image of standing behind the line, then widens to the minus column of a decision, to whole populations lacking resources, to a handicap imposed for fairness, and finally to the verb of taking an advantage away. In every sense the question is the same: who is further back, and why?
sensesIntro.cn: disadvantage 首先是位置词，其次才是道德词。它从“站在线后”的意象出发，扩展到决策的减分栏、缺少资源的整群人、为求公平而施加的让步，最后到“撤走优势”的动词。每个义项问的都是同一件事：谁更靠后，为什么？

core.en: Standing behind the line: an advantage removed or missing.
core.cn: 站在线后：一份被撤走或缺失的优势。

branches.en: ASSESSMENT: a condition, a drawback, a point against an argument.
branches.cn: 评估：一种条件、一个缺点、一条不利于论点的理由。

branches.en: SOCIETY: deprivation that holds groups and learners back.
branches.cn: 社会：拖住群体与学习者的资源缺失。

branches.en: POSITION: at a disadvantage, and a handicap conceded in sport.
branches.cn: 位置：处于不利地位，以及体育中让出的劣势。

branches.en: MARKET: a relative weakness against rivals.
branches.cn: 市场：相对竞争对手的弱势。

branches.en: ACTION: the verb of putting someone at a disadvantage.
branches.cn: 动作：使某人处于不利地位的动词。

intro.en: Disadvantage is a prefix plus a French noun. The items show the privative dis- at work, and contrast it with the separating dis- of diffusion and the intensifying dis- of disturb.
intro.cn: disadvantage 是一个前缀加一个法语名词。下列条目展示否定性 dis- 的作用，并与 diffusion 中表分开的 dis-、disturb 中表加强的 dis- 对照。

latinIntro.en: The Latin phrase ab ante is the origin of avant and advantage. It is a phrase rather than a single word, which is why advantage has no neat Latin root noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁短语 ab ante 是 avant 与 advantage 的来源。它是短语而非单词，这正是 advantage 没有一个整齐的拉丁词根名词的原因。

items.meaning: an unfavourable condition; to put at a disadvantage
items.meaningCN: 不利条件；使处于不利地位
items.example: Cost is the chief disadvantage of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 成本是这个方案的主要缺点。

items.example: Speed is our main advantage.
items.exampleCN: 速度是我们的主要优势。

items.example: The scholarship helps disadvantaged students.
items.exampleCN: 这项奖学金帮助弱势学生。

items.example: The terms were disadvantageous to buyers.
Advantaged groups resist redistributive taxes.
items.exampleCN: 处于优势的群体抵制再分配税。

items.example: The army advanced before dawn.

items.meaning: in a way that creates a disadvantage
items.example: The clause was disadvantageously drafted.
items.exampleCN: 这一条款起草得对己不利。

items.example: Few writers use disadvantageousness.
items.exampleCN: 很少作者使用 disadvantageousness 一词。

items.structure: aphetic form of advantage, from avant
items.meaning: a position giving a good view
items.example: From this vantage the whole valley is visible.
items.exampleCN: 从这个位置能看见整个山谷。

definition_zh: 消失；不见；失踪；灭绝；（症状）消退
definition_en: the fact or process of something no longer being visible, present or in existence
core_image: 舞台上一个人走进黑幕，灯光移开，台上只剩下空的轮廓
scene: 舞台边，魔术师把一只箱子盖上布，灯一暗再亮，箱子和助手都不见了。The magician drapes a cloth over the box, the lights go out and come back, and the box and the assistant are gone: a disappearance.
sceneCN: 这里 disappearance 是「消失不见」（第 1、7 个义项：不可见与魔术消失）；句意：魔术师把布盖在箱子上，灯一暗再亮，箱子和助手都不见了，这就是一次消失。图中可辨识物件：舞台、盖布、空箱子位置、观众席。

derivatives.zh: 令人失望的（同前缀不同词根，勿混）

senses.title: Going out of sight
senses.definition: the act of passing from being visible to being invisible
senses.definitionCN: 从可见变为不可见的行为
senses.example: The sudden disappearance of the sun behind clouds surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳突然消失在云后，让我们吃了一惊。
senses.why: Latin apparere is ad- 'toward' plus parere 'come into view'. Disappearance adds the privative dis-, so the coming-into-view is undone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 apparere 是 ad-“朝向”加 parere“进入视野”。disappearance 加否定性 dis-，把“进入视野”这件事撤销。

senses.title: A person going missing
senses.definition: the unexplained absence of a person whose whereabouts are unknown
senses.definitionCN: 一个人下落不明、无法解释的缺席
senses.example: Police are investigating the disappearance of the hiker.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正在调查这名徒步者的失踪。
senses.why: A person who should appear somewhere does not. The word is deliberately neutral: it reports absence without saying whether it was voluntary or forced.
senses.whyCN: 一个本该出现在某处的人没有出现。这个词刻意保持中立：它报告缺席，但不说明是自愿还是被迫。

senses.title: A species dying out
senses.definition: the loss of all living members of a species from the world
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种的全部存活个体从世界上消失
senses.example: The disappearance of large mammals followed the loss of habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 大型哺乳动物的消失伴随着栖息地的丧失。
senses.why: The word is gentler than extinction: it describes what an observer can confirm, that the animals are no longer found, without claiming to know the final cause.
senses.whyCN: 这个词比 extinction 温和：它描述观察者能确认的事实——这些动物再也找不到了，而不宣称知道最终原因。

senses.title: Records or evidence vanishing
senses.definition: the loss or removal of documents, data or objects that should be available
senses.definitionCN: 本应可取的文书、数据或物品的丢失或被移除
senses.example: The disappearance of the files delayed the inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 文件的消失延误了调查。
senses.why: Here what vanishes is not a body but a trace. The word carries suspicion because records seldom vanish on their own.
senses.whyCN: 这里消失的不是身体，而是痕迹。因为记录很少自行消失，这个词带着怀疑的意味。

senses.title: A practice or language fading
senses.definition: the gradual ending of a custom, skill or language as it stops being used
senses.definitionCN: 习俗、技艺或语言因不再被使用而逐渐终结
senses.example: The disappearance of the dialect took three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方言的消失历经三代人。
senses.why: A language does not die in one moment; its speakers simply stop appearing. The word fits gradual, unattributable loss better than any single cause.
senses.whyCN: 一种语言不会一瞬间死去；只是说它的人渐渐不再出现。对于这种渐进的、无单一原因的丧失，这个词最贴切。

senses.title: A signal or substance leaving a system
senses.titleCN: 信号或物质从系统中消失
senses.definition: in science, the point at which a measurable signal, substance or feature is no longer detected
senses.definitionCN: 科学中可测的信号、物质或特征不再被检测到的时点
senses.example: The disappearance of the tracer marked the end of the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 示踪物的消失标志着反应结束。
senses.why: Instruments report presence or absence, not essence. The word is chosen in lab writing because it sticks to what the measurement shows.
senses.whyCN: 仪器报告的是有无，而不是本质。实验写作选用这个词，正因为它只停留在测量显示的东西上。

senses.title: A magician's vanishing trick
senses.definition: an illusion in which an object or person seems to vanish from the stage
senses.definitionCN: 一种错觉表演，使物体或人似乎从舞台上消失
senses.example: The audience gasped at the disappearance of the assistant.
senses.exampleCN: 观众为助手的消失倒吸一口气。
senses.why: The trick works by controlling sight, not by removing the object. The word names what the eye reports, which is exactly why it suits a stage illusion.
senses.whyCN: 戏法靠控制视线，而不是真的移走物体。这个词命名的是眼睛报告的东西，正因如此才适合舞台错觉。

senses.title: Forced disappearance as a violation
senses.definition: in law and human rights, the secret detention or abduction of a person by state agents or others acting with their support
senses.definitionCN: 法律与人权语境中由国家人员或其支持者秘密拘禁或绑架某人
senses.example: The treaty criminalizes enforced disappearance.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约将强迫失踪定为犯罪。
senses.why: Here the neutrality of 'absence' is turned into an accusation. The person is made to disappear by someone, and the passive form hides the agent.
senses.whyCN: 这里“缺席”的中立性被转为指控。人是被某人弄得消失的，而被动形式恰恰隐藏了施动者。

senses.title: Symptoms clearing up
senses.definition: in medicine, the clearing of a sign or symptom after treatment or recovery
senses.definitionCN: 医学中体征或症状在治疗或康复后消失
senses.example: The disappearance of the rash confirmed the diagnosis.
senses.exampleCN: 皮疹的消退印证了诊断。
senses.why: Medical writing prefers disappearance to cure because it describes the observed change, not the underlying mechanism. The rash is no longer there; why is a separate question.
senses.whyCN: 医学写作偏好 disappearance 而非 cure，因为它描述观察到的变化，而非底层机制。皮疹不在了；为什么不在，是另一个问题。

intro.en: Disappearance is dis- plus the noun of appear. Appear comes from Latin apparere, ad- 'toward' plus parere 'come into view'. The English noun is a 17th-century formation, built when the verb disappear had already settled.
intro.cn: disappearance 是 dis- 加 appear 的名词。appear 来自拉丁 apparere，即 ad-“朝向”加 parere“进入视野”。这个英语名词是 17 世纪的构造，成型时动词 disappear 已经稳定。

items.en: The root *per- meant 'to bring forth, to produce'. Latin parere 'to come forth, to appear' comes from it, and so does the unrelated-looking parent, 'one who brings forth'.
items.cn: 词根 *per- 意为“带出、产生”。拉丁 parere“出现、显现”由此而来；看似无关的 parent“生育者”也同出此源。

items.en: Parere could mean 'to appear' or 'to obey'; the two senses are separate developments. With ad-, apparere meant 'to come into view', the source of appear and appearance.
items.cn: parere 既有“出现”也有“服从”义，两者是各自发展的结果。加 ad- 后，apparere 意为“进入视野”，是 appear 与 appearance 的来源。

items.en: Old French aparoir gave English appear; its negative desaparoir gave disappear. The prefix was assimilated to English dis- in spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 aparoir 给出英语 appear；其否定形式 desaparoir 给出 disappear。前缀在拼写上被英语化为 dis-。

items.en: Disappear is recorded in the 15th century, at first of things going out of sight. The sense of a person missing is later and harder to date.
items.cn: disappear 在 15 世纪有记录，最初指事物离开视野。指人失踪的义项出现更晚，也更难确定年代。

items.en: The noun disappearance follows in the 17th century, formed with -ance on the model of appearance. Both words keep the same suffix, so the pair stays symmetrical.
items.cn: 名词 disappearance 随后在 17 世纪出现，仿 appearance 加 -ance 构成。两词共用同一后缀，因此这一对保持对称。

items.en: Enforced disappearance becomes a term of international law after the 1970s, while scientific writing adopts disappearance for any signal that is no longer detected.
items.cn: 强迫失踪在 1970 年代后成为国际法术语，而科学写作则用 disappearance 指任何不再被检测到的信号。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, its positive counterpart and a false friend with the same prefix. The meaning group contrasts vanishing with extinction, loss and absence.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、其肯定对应词，以及同前缀的假朋友；词义组把“消失”与“灭绝”“丢失”“缺席”区分开。

entries.definition: to go out of sight or cease to exist. The noun adds -ance to it.
entries.definitionCN: 离开视野或不再存在。名词在其上加 -ance。

entries.definition: the act of coming into view, or the look of someone. It shares the suffix and reverses the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 进入视野的行为，或某人的外貌。它共用后缀，前缀相反。

entries.definition: causing disappointment, from appoint, not from appear. The shared dis- does not make them relatives.
entries.definitionCN: 令人失望的，来自 appoint 而非 appear。共用的 dis- 并不使它们同源。

entries.definition: the complete dying out of a species. It is stronger and more final than disappearance, which may only report that none are found.
entries.definitionCN: 某一物种完全灭绝。它比 disappearance 更强、更终局，后者只报告找不到。

entries.definition: the state of not being present. It is static, while disappearance implies a change from present to absent.
entries.definitionCN: 不在场的状态。它是静态的，而 disappearance 暗示从在场变为不在。

entries.definition: the fact of no longer having something. It stresses ownership and grief, while disappearance stresses the vanishing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 不再拥有某物的事实。它强调所有权与失落，而 disappearance 强调消失本身。

entries.definition: the act of fading from sight, often used of things that leave no trace. It is more literary than disappearance.
entries.definitionCN: 从视野中淡去的行为，常用于不留痕迹的事物。它比 disappearance 更文学化。

entries.definition: the change of a liquid into vapour. It is one physical mechanism by which something can disappear.
entries.definitionCN: 液体变为蒸气。它是事物消失的一种物理机制。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from appear and its privative prefix, then let the stage image stretch to people, species and evidence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 appear 与否定前缀搭起这个词，再用舞台意象扩展到人、物种与证据。

normal.en: See dis- + appear: the coming-into-view is switched off.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 appear：“进入视野”被关掉。

normal.en: Keep the magician image: the eye is fooled, and the word reports what the eye says.
normal.cn: 记住魔术师意象：眼睛被骗，而这个词只报告眼睛所说的。

normal.en: For a missing person, notice the neutrality: the word hides whether it was voluntary.
normal.cn: 指人失踪时，注意它的中立：这个词不说是否自愿。

normal.en: For species, prefer disappearance when you only know they are no longer found.
normal.cn: 指物种时，若只知道再也找不到，就用 disappearance。

normal.en: Keep its twin in view: appearance adds, disappearance removes, same -ance.
normal.cn: 盯着它的双胞胎：appearance 加上，disappearance 撤走，同一个 -ance。

abstract.en: Reduce the word to one operation: visibility subtracted. Everything else is a special case of that subtraction.
abstract.cn: 把词缩成一个操作：可见性被减去。其余义项都是这个减法的特例。

abstract.en: Notice that the word always needs a witness: someone must have expected the thing to be there.
abstract.cn: 注意这个词总需要一个见证者：必须有人本以为那东西会在。

abstract.en: Separate the two questions every sense hides: is it gone, or is it merely unseen?
abstract.cn: 把每个义项藏着的两个问题分开：它是真的没了，还是只是没被看见？

examples.en: The disappearance of the bees alarmed local farmers.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂的消失让当地农民感到惊慌。

examples.en: Investigators could not explain the disappearance of the original documents.
examples.cn: 调查人员无法解释原始文件的失踪。

examples.en: After treatment, the disappearance of the fever was rapid.
examples.cn: 治疗后，发烧很快消退。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地思阿皮尔人死”：地上想着那个叫皮尔的人死了、不见了——disappearance 就是消失、失踪。

root: 拉丁语 apparere“进入视野”（ad- 朝向 + parere 显现），经古法语 aparoir 进入英语作 appear；其否定形式 desaparoir 给出 disappear，加 -ance 构成 disappearance。注意 parere 另有“服从”义，与“显现”义为同形异义。

sensesIntro.en: Disappearance is appearance with a minus sign. It always presupposes a witness who expected the thing to be present: a sun behind a cloud, a hiker who never arrives, a species no longer trapped, a file no longer in its drawer, a rash no longer on the skin. The nine senses move from literal sight to legal accusation and clinical observation, but each reports the same event: something that should be there is not.
sensesIntro.cn: disappearance 就是加了负号的 appearance。它总预设一个见证者，此人本以为那东西会在：云后的太阳、没有抵达的徒步者、再也捕不到的物种、不在抽屉里的文件、皮肤上不再有的皮疹。九个义项从字面的视觉走到法律指控与临床观察，但每一个报告的都是同一件事：本该在那里的东西不在。

core.en: Visibility subtracted: what should be seen is not seen.
core.cn: 可见性被减去：本该被看见的没被看见。

branches.en: SIGHT: going out of view, and the stage trick that fakes it.
branches.cn: 视觉：离开视野，以及伪造它的舞台戏法。

branches.en: PERSONS: unexplained absence and enforced removal.
branches.cn: 人：无法解释的缺席与强迫消失。

branches.en: WORLD: species, languages and customs fading away.
branches.cn: 世界：物种、语言与习俗的消逝。

branches.en: TRACES: documents and evidence that should still exist.
branches.cn: 痕迹：本应仍存在的文件与证据。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: signals no longer detected, symptoms no longer present.
branches.cn: 测量：不再被检测的信号，不再存在的症状。

intro.en: Disappearance is dis- plus appear plus -ance. The items show the same -ance suffix on other verbs, and show that dis- can negate, separate or intensify depending on the base.
intro.cn: disappearance 是 dis- 加 appear 再加 -ance。下列条目展示同一 -ance 后缀用于其他动词，并展示 dis- 依词基不同可以表否定、分开或加强。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are the verb of coming into view and two of its relatives. They make clear that 'appear' and 'obey' share a spelling in Latin but not a meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“进入视野”的动词及其两个亲属。它们说明 appear 与“服从”在拉丁语中拼写相同，但意义不同。

items.meaning: the fact of vanishing or going missing
items.example: The disappearance of the keys delayed everyone.
items.exampleCN: 钥匙的消失耽误了所有人。

items.meaning: to go out of sight; to cease to exist
items.example: The fog disappeared by noon.

items.meaning: to come into view; to seem
items.example: A figure appeared at the door.

items.meaning: the act of appearing; outward look
items.example: His appearance surprised the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 他的到场让会议吃了一惊。

items.meaning: clearly visible; seeming rather than real
items.example: The cause was apparent to everyone.
items.exampleCN: 原因对每个人都显而易见。

items.example: The glass is completely transparent.
They reported an apparition in the corridor.
items.exampleCN: 他们报告走廊里有幽灵显现。

items.example: The cause was unapparent at first.
The ending disappointed many readers.
items.exampleCN: 这个结局让许多读者失望。

definition_zh: 纪律的；惩戒的；学科的；规训的
definition_en: relating to rules and punishment, or to a branch of study and its methods
core_image: 一张桌子两边：一边放着行为守则与处罚条例，一边放着学科书目与方法手册
scene: 学院走廊里，墙上并排挂着两块牌子，一块写守则与处罚，一块写本领域的研究方法。Two notices hang side by side in the corridor: one lists conduct and penalties, the other the methods of the field, and both fall under disciplinary rules.
sceneCN: 这里 disciplinary 是「纪律惩戒的；学科的」（第 1、2 个义项：规则处罚与学科归属）；句意：走廊里并排挂着两块牌子，一块写守则与处罚，一块写本领域的方法，都归在纪律与学科之下。图中可辨识物件：走廊、两块牌子、守则文本、学科书目。

pos.zh: 纪律的；惩戒的；学科的；规训的

senses.title: Relating to rules and punishment
senses.definition: concerned with the enforcement of rules and the punishment of those who break them
senses.definitionCN: 与规则的执行及对违规者的处罚有关的
senses.example: The committee opened a disciplinary inquiry into the complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会就该投诉启动了纪律调查。
senses.why: Latin disciplina meant 'instruction' before it meant 'punishment'. Disciplinary keeps the older frame: rules exist to train, and penalties are the last instrument of that training.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 disciplina 先指“教导”，后指“惩罚”。disciplinary 保留了较早的框架：规则是为了训练，处罚只是这种训练的最后手段。

senses.title: Belonging to a field of study
senses.definition: relating to a branch of knowledge, its methods and its standards of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 与某一知识分支、其方法及证据标准有关的
senses.example: The paper crosses disciplinary boundaries between biology and economics.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文跨越了生物学与经济学之间的学科边界。
senses.why: A discipline is first a body of instruction. A field of study is exactly that: a body of things taught and methods passed on. The academic sense is older than it looks.
senses.whyCN: discipline 首先是一套教导。一个研究领域正是如此：一套被教的东西与传下去的方法。这个学术义比看上去更古老。

senses.title: Formal proceedings against a member
senses.titleCN: 对成员的正式纪律程序
senses.definition: describing an official process by which a professional body investigates and may penalize a member
senses.definitionCN: 描述专业团体调查并可能处罚成员的正式程序
senses.example: The nurse faced a disciplinary hearing over the error.
senses.exampleCN: 这名护士因该失误面临纪律听证。
senses.why: Here the adjective marks a procedure, not a mood. Disciplinary hearing is a fixed phrase because the hearing exists only to apply the rules of the profession.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词标记的是一套程序，而不是一种气氛。disciplinary hearing 是固定搭配，因为这种听证只为执行行业规则而存在。

senses.title: Training that produces self-control
senses.definition: relating to the training of habits, obedience or self-control
senses.definitionCN: 与习惯、服从或自制的训练有关的
senses.example: Sport offers disciplinary training in patience.
senses.exampleCN: 运动提供了耐心的纪律训练。
senses.why: The root discere means 'to learn'. Disciplinary training is not primarily about catching offenders; it is about making a behaviour reliable through repetition.
senses.whyCN: 词根 discere 意为“学习”。纪律训练主要不是抓违规者，而是通过重复让某种行为变得可靠。

senses.title: Self-imposed ascetic practice
senses.definition: relating to strict self-regulation, especially in religious or ascetic practice
senses.definitionCN: 与严格自我约束有关的，尤指宗教或苦修实践
senses.example: The monastery kept a disciplinary silence after compline.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院在晚祷后保持纪律性的静默。
senses.why: Religious orders used disciplina for the rule that shaped a life. The disciplinary silence is not a punishment for anyone; it is the rule itself acting on the body.
senses.whyCN: 修会用 disciplina 指塑造生活的会规。纪律性的静默不是对谁的惩罚；它就是会规本身作用在身体上。

senses.title: Governing by surveillance and correction
senses.definition: in social theory, describing power that shapes behaviour through observation, normalization and correction
senses.definitionCN: 社会理论中描述通过观察、规范化与纠正来塑造行为的权力
senses.example: Foucault described the disciplinary power of schools and prisons.
senses.exampleCN: 福柯描述了学校与监狱的规训权力。
senses.why: This sense stresses that rules do not only punish after the fact; they produce docile bodies by constant watching. The adjective shifts from 'of rules' to 'of a mode of power'.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项强调规则不只事后惩罚；它们通过持续观看生产驯顺的身体。形容词从“规则的”转向“一种权力模式的”。

senses.title: A board that applies the rules
senses.definition: describing a body, such as a board or tribunal, whose function is to apply professional or institutional rules
senses.definitionCN: 描述以执行专业或机构规则为职能的机构，如委员会或裁判庭
senses.example: The disciplinary board meets on the first Monday of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 纪律委员会每月第一个星期一开会。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to institutions rather than to acts. A disciplinary board is defined by its function, not by the severity of its decisions.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词附着在机构上，而不是行为上。纪律委员会由其职能定义，而不是由其决定的严厉程度定义。

senses.title: Methods specific to a field
senses.definition: describing the techniques, vocabulary and standards that a particular academic field treats as proper
senses.definitionCN: 描述某一学术领域视为正当的技术、词汇与标准
senses.example: Peer review is a disciplinary norm, not a universal one.
senses.exampleCN: 同行评议是一种学科规范，而非普世规范。
senses.why: Each field trains its members to see some evidence as decisive and other evidence as irrelevant. What counts as proof is itself disciplinary.
senses.whyCN: 每个领域都训练其成员把某些证据看作决定性的，把另一些看作无关的。什么算作证明，本身就是学科性的。

intro.en: Disciplinary is discipline plus -ary. Discipline comes from Latin disciplina, 'instruction, knowledge, a rule of life', from discipulus 'pupil', from discere 'to learn'. The adjective is a 16th-century formation and carries both the teaching and the punishing branches.
intro.cn: disciplinary 是 discipline 加 -ary。discipline 来自拉丁 disciplina“教导、知识、生活规则”，源于 discipulus“学生”，再上溯 discere“学习”。形容词是 16 世纪构造，同时承载“教导”与“惩罚”两支。

items.en: The root *dek- meant 'to take, to accept'. Latin discere 'to learn' comes from it, and so does docere 'to teach', which supplies doctor and document.
items.cn: 词根 *dek- 意为“拿取、接受”。拉丁 discere“学习”由此而来，docere“教导”也同出此源，后者给出 doctor 与 document。

items.en: Discere meant 'to learn'. Discipulus, 'pupil', is generally taken as discere plus a suffix; some handbooks link the ending to capere 'to grasp'. The exact formation is marked here as source uncertain.
items.cn: discere 意为“学习”。discipulus“学生”一般认为由 discere 加后缀构成；部分手册把词尾联系到 capere“抓取”。确切构词在此标注为「来源不确定」。

items.en: Disciplina covered instruction, a branch of knowledge, and the rule by which a pupil lives. Roman writers used it for military training as well, which prepared the later sense of enforced order.
items.cn: disciplina 涵盖教导、知识分支以及学生所遵循的规则。罗马作家也用它指军事训练，为后来“强制秩序”的义项铺路。

items.en: Old French discipline entered English as discipline with the senses 'instruction' and 'rule'. The punitive sense grows in the 16th century as institutions formalize penalties.
items.cn: 古法语 discipline 进入英语作 discipline，带“教导”与“规则”义。随着机构把处罚制度化，惩罚义在 16 世纪生长起来。

items.en: The adjective disciplinary is formed to mean 'of or belonging to discipline'. Early uses concern church and school order rather than academic fields.
items.cn: 形容词 disciplinary 构成，意为“属于 discipline 的”。早期用法关于教会与学校秩序，而非学术领域。

items.en: As universities organized into departments, disciplinary came to mean 'belonging to a field of study', and interdisciplinary followed. In the 20th century social theory gave it the sense of a mode of power.
items.cn: 随着大学按系科组织，disciplinary 开始表示“属于某一研究领域”，interdisciplinary 随之出现。20 世纪的社会理论又赋予它“一种权力模式”的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun, the person noun and the adjective of state. The meaning group contrasts rule-enforcement with academic and corrective terms.
note.cn: 形近组区分名词、指人名词与状态形容词；词义组把“执行规则”与学术、纠正类词区分开。

entries.definition: a field of study, a system of rules, or the act of training and punishing. All senses of the adjective come from it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究领域、规则体系，或训练与处罚行为。形容词的所有义项都来自它。

entries.definition: a person who insists on strict rules. It names a person, while disciplinary describes rules or procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持严格规则的人。它指人，而 disciplinary 描述规则或程序。

entries.definition: trained to obey and control oneself. It describes a person's habit, not an institution's function.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、能服从与自控的。它描述个人习惯，而非机构职能。

entries.definition: intended as punishment. It is narrower than disciplinary, which also covers instruction and academic fields.
entries.definitionCN: 以惩罚为目的的。它比 disciplinary 窄，后者还涵盖教导与学科。

entries.definition: intended to correct a fault. A corrective measure aims at repair, while a disciplinary one aims at order.
entries.definitionCN: 意在纠正错误的。纠正措施目标是修复，纪律措施目标是秩序。

entries.definition: relating to study and scholarship. It overlaps with sense 02 but says nothing about rules or punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 与学习和学术有关的。它与第 2 义项重叠，但不涉及规则或处罚。

entries.definition: relating to official rules and their administration. It stresses formal regulation more than training.
entries.definitionCN: 与官方规则及其执行有关的。它比训练更强调正式规章。

entries.definition: relating to the methods of a field. It is close to sense 08 but focuses on procedure rather than standards.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一领域的方法有关的。它接近第 8 义项，但聚焦于程序而非标准。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into the learning root and the adjective suffix, then place the two main branches side by side: rules and fields.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成“学习”词根与形容词后缀，再把两大分支并排放好：规则与学科。

normal.en: See discere, 'to learn', behind discipline: rules began as lessons.
normal.cn: 看见 discipline 背后的 discere“学习”：规则最初是课程。

normal.en: Picture the two noticeboards: penalties on one, reading lists on the other, both labelled disciplinary.
normal.cn: 想象那两块告示牌：一边是处罚，一边是书单，都写着 disciplinary。

normal.en: For a professional, disciplinary hearing is a procedure, not an insult.
normal.cn: 对专业人士来说，纪律听证是一套程序，不是侮辱。

normal.en: For academia, remember interdisciplinary: fields have borders, so they can be crossed.
normal.cn: 学术方面记住 interdisciplinary：学科有边界，所以能被跨越。

normal.en: Keep the old monastic image: silence kept as a rule, not as a punishment.
normal.cn: 记住古老的修院意象：静默是作为会规而守，不是作为惩罚。

abstract.en: Hold one axis with two ends: training at one end, punishment at the other, and most uses sit between.
abstract.cn: 抓住一根轴的两端：一端是训练，一端是惩罚，多数用法位于中间。

abstract.en: Notice that a discipline is both a thing you learn and a thing that constrains you.
abstract.cn: 注意 discipline 既是你要学的东西，也是约束你的东西。

abstract.en: Ask of every use: is the rule shaping a person, or sorting knowledge?
abstract.cn: 对每个用法都问：这条规则在塑造人，还是在整理知识？

examples.en: The company took disciplinary action against two employees.
examples.cn: 公司对两名员工采取了纪律处分。

examples.en: Her work is admired across disciplinary lines.
examples.cn: 她的研究跨越学科界限而受到赞赏。

examples.en: The journal applies strict disciplinary standards to submissions.
examples.cn: 该刊对投稿采用严格的学科标准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯普林那里”：地里的斯普林（discipline）在那边立着牌子，一边写纪律，一边写学科——disciplinary 就是纪律的、学科的。

root: 拉丁语 discere“学习”，派生 discipulus“学生”（构词细节存疑），再派生 disciplina“教导、知识、生活规则”；经古法语 discipline 进入英语，加形容词后缀 -ary 构成 disciplinary。同根 docere“教导”给出 doctor、document、docile。

sensesIntro.en: Disciplinary holds two branches that grew from one trunk. The trunk is disciplina, a body of instruction; one branch became the rules a learner must obey, the other became the field a learner studies. From the first come hearings, penalties and the theory of disciplinary power; from the second come boundaries, methods and interdisciplinary work. The adjective is always about a frame that shapes people or knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: disciplinary 的两大分支长在同一根主干上。主干是 disciplina，一套教导；一支长成学习者必须遵守的规则，另一支长成学习者所研究的领域。前者给出听证、处罚与规训权力理论；后者给出学科边界、方法与跨学科工作。这个形容词始终关于一个塑造人或知识的框架。

core.en: A frame of instruction: rules that train, and fields that organize knowledge.
core.cn: 一套教导框架：训练人的规则，以及整理知识的学科。

branches.en: ENFORCEMENT: rules, hearings and the boards that apply them.
branches.cn: 执行：规则、听证与执行规则的机构。

branches.en: SCHOLARSHIP: fields, their boundaries, methods and standards.
branches.cn: 学术：领域、边界、方法与标准。

branches.en: TRAINING: habit made reliable by repetition.
branches.cn: 训练：通过重复使习惯变得可靠。

branches.en: ASCETIC RULE: self-imposed order shaping a life.
branches.cn: 苦修会规：塑造生活的自我约束。

branches.en: THEORY: power that shapes behaviour by watching it.
branches.cn: 理论：通过观看塑造行为的权力。

intro.en: Disciplinary is a noun plus -ary. The items show the discere family, the person suffix -arian, and the productive prefix inter- that turns a discipline into a crossing.
intro.cn: disciplinary 是名词加 -ary。下列条目展示 discere 词族、指人后缀 -arian，以及把学科变成“跨越”的高产前缀 inter-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries pair discere with docere, the two halves of teaching. One is what the pupil does, the other what the teacher does.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目把 discere 与 docere 放在一起，这是教学的两半：一个是学生做的，一个是教师做的。

items.meaning: relating to rules, punishment or a field of study
items.meaningCN: 与规则、处罚或学科有关的
items.example: The matter went to a disciplinary panel.
items.exampleCN: 此事交由纪律小组处理。

items.meaning: training; a field of study; a system of rules
items.example: History is an old discipline.
items.exampleCN: 历史学是一门古老的学科。

items.meaning: a person who insists on strict rules
items.example: The headmaster was a strict disciplinarian.
items.exampleCN: 校长是一位严格纪律的执行者。

items.meaning: trained to obey and control oneself
items.example: She kept a disciplined study routine.
items.exampleCN: 她保持有纪律的学习作息。

items.example: The centre runs interdisciplinary research.
items.exampleCN: 该中心开展跨学科研究。

items.meaning: drawing on several fields side by side
items.example: The clinic uses a multidisciplinary team.
items.exampleCN: 该诊所使用多学科团队。

items.meaning: a follower who learns from a teacher
items.example: He was a disciple of the old master.
items.exampleCN: 他是那位老大师的弟子。

items.example: The animal was remarkably docile.

items.meaning: a teacher; a holder of the highest degree
items.example: She earned her doctorate in physics.
items.exampleCN: 她获得了物理学博士学位。

definition_zh: 披露；揭露；公开的信息；自我表露
definition_en: the act of making something known that was private, secret or not previously public
core_image: 一张密封的文件袋被拆开封口，里面的纸摊在桌上给所有人看
scene: 会议室里，财务主管把一只封了蜡的文件袋拆开，把里面的账目摊在桌上。In the meeting room the finance director breaks the wax seal, spreads the accounts on the table and calls it full disclosure.
