sceneCN: 这里 disclosure 是「披露、公开信息」（第 1、3 个义项：公开与财务披露）；句意：财务主管拆开封蜡，把账目全部摊在桌上，称为完全披露。图中可辨识物件：文件袋、封蜡、账目表、会议桌。

pos.zh: 披露；揭露；公开的信息；自我表露

derivatives.zh: 关闭；结束（同词根，义相反方向）
围住；把……装入（en- 使进入）

senses.title: Opening what was closed
senses.titleCN: 把封闭的东西打开给人看
senses.definition: the act of making known something that was previously hidden or private
senses.definitionCN: 把此前隐藏或私密的东西公开的行为
senses.example: The disclosure of the letters changed the historical record.
senses.exampleCN: 这些书信的披露改变了历史记载。
senses.why: Latin disclaudere is dis- 'apart' plus claudere 'to shut'. A disclosure is literally an un-shutting: the cover is taken off and the contents are exposed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 disclaudere 是 dis-“分开”加 claudere“关闭”。disclosure 字面就是“打开”：盖子被拿开，内容露出来。

senses.title: The fact that is revealed
senses.definition: a piece of information that has been brought to public attention
senses.definitionCN: 被带到公众注意之下的一条信息
senses.example: The report contained several shocking disclosures.
senses.exampleCN: 报告中有几项令人震惊的揭露。
senses.why: English allows process nouns to name their own results. What is disclosed becomes a disclosure, just as a finding becomes a discovery.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许过程名词指称自身的结果。被披露的内容也就成了一个 disclosure，正如 a finding 成为一个 discovery。

senses.title: Companies publishing their accounts
senses.definition: in business and law, the publication of financial and other material facts by a company
senses.definitionCN: 商业与法律中公司公布财务及其他重要事实
senses.example: Investors relied on the annual disclosure.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者依赖年度披露。
senses.why: A listed company is legally required to un-shut its books. Disclosure here is a duty, not a favour, and its scope is defined by regulators.
senses.whyCN: 上市公司被法律要求打开账本。这里的披露是一项义务，不是恩惠，其范围由监管者界定。

senses.title: Handing over documents in litigation
senses.definition: in law, the compulsory revelation of documents and evidence to the other party before trial
senses.definitionCN: 法律中审判前向对方强制揭示文件与证据
senses.example: The court ordered full disclosure of the correspondence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令完全开示相关通信。
senses.why: A trial is unfair if one side holds closed files. Disclosure is the procedural un-shutting that lets both parties see the same record.
senses.whyCN: 如果一方握着封闭的文件，审判就不公平。disclosure 就是程序上的“打开”，让双方看到同一份记录。

senses.title: Telling others about oneself
senses.definition: in psychology, the act of revealing personal information about oneself to another person
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中向他人透露关于自己的私人信息
senses.example: Gradual self-disclosure builds trust between strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 渐进的自我表露在陌生人之间建立信任。
senses.why: The closed thing here is the self. Self-disclosure is the deliberate opening of a private interior, and its pace measures intimacy.
senses.whyCN: 这里被封闭的东西是自我。自我表露是有意打开私密的内部，其节奏衡量着亲密程度。

senses.title: Declaring a conflict of interest
senses.definition: the formal statement of a personal interest that might bias a judgement or decision
senses.definitionCN: 对可能影响判断或决定的个人利益作出正式说明
senses.example: The reviewer filed a conflict-of-interest disclosure.
senses.exampleCN: 评审人提交了利益冲突披露。
senses.why: The disclosure does not remove the conflict; it makes it visible so others can weigh the judgement. Openness substitutes for purity.
senses.whyCN: 披露并不消除利益冲突；它让冲突可见，以便他人权衡判断。公开替代了纯洁。

senses.title: Government opening its records
senses.definition: in public administration, the release of official information to citizens on request or by policy
senses.definitionCN: 公共行政中应请求或按政策向公民发布官方信息
senses.example: Freedom-of-information laws widen government disclosure.
senses.exampleCN: 信息自由法扩大了政府的信息公开。
senses.why: Here the closed drawer belongs to the state. Disclosure becomes a democratic mechanism: the public can check what was done in its name.
senses.whyCN: 这里封闭的抽屉属于国家。披露成为一种民主机制：公众可以核查以自己名义做了什么。

senses.title: Openness with no reservation
senses.definition: the state of hiding nothing relevant, especially in the phrase full disclosure
senses.definitionCN: 不隐瞒任何相关事项的状态，尤用于短语 full disclosure
senses.example: Full disclosure requires mentioning the failed trial too.
senses.exampleCN: 完全披露也要求提到那次失败的试验。
senses.why: Full disclosure is a standard rather than an act: every relevant drawer must be opened. The adjective sets the completeness, the noun the opening.
senses.whyCN: full disclosure 是一个标准而非一次动作：每个相关抽屉都必须打开。形容词规定完整度，名词规定打开。

senses.title: A formal statement that discloses
senses.definition: a document or section of a document in which required information is set out
senses.definitionCN: 载明所需信息的文件或文件中的一节
senses.example: Read the risk disclosure before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签署前请阅读风险披露声明。
senses.why: The noun shifts from the act to the paper that performs it. A disclosure statement is the institutional form of the un-shutting.
senses.whyCN: 名词从行为转向执行该行为的纸张。披露声明是“打开”这一动作的制度化形式。

intro.en: Disclosure is dis- plus close plus -ure. Close comes from Latin claudere 'to shut', through Old French clos. The verb disclose existed in English by the 14th century, and the noun followed with the French-style suffix -ure.
intro.cn: disclosure 是 dis- 加 close 再加 -ure。close 来自拉丁 claudere“关闭”，经古法语 clos 传入。动词 disclose 在 14 世纪已见于英语，名词随后以法语式后缀 -ure 构成。

items.en: Claudere meant 'to shut, to close'. Its past participle clausus supplies clause, close, cloister and the -clud- of include and exclude.
items.cn: claudere 意为“关闭”。其过去分词 clausus 给出 clause、close、cloister，以及 include、exclude 中的 -clud-。

items.en: Classical Latin had no common verb *disclaudere; the negative verb took shape in Romance. Old French built desclore from des- plus clore, and English borrowed that form. The Latin reconstruction is marked here as a reconstructed form, not an attested classical verb.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语并无常见的 *disclaudere 动词，否定形式是在罗曼语中成形的。古法语用 des- 加 clore 构成 desclore，英语借入这一形式。此处的拉丁重构仅作“重构形式”标注，并非古典拉丁语中实际可查的动词。

items.en: Old French desclore meant 'to open up, to reveal'. Its stem supplied Middle English disclosen, later disclose.
items.cn: 古法语 desclore 意为“打开、揭示”。其词干给出中古英语 disclosen，后作 disclose。

items.en: The verb appears in the 14th century with the sense 'to open up, to expose to view'. It is used of secrets, wounds and enclosed places alike.
items.cn: 动词在 14 世纪出现，意为“打开、使显露”。它既用于秘密，也用于伤口与围合之处。

items.en: The noun is formed with -ure, the same suffix as in closure and exposure. Early uses concern the act of revealing; the 'thing revealed' sense follows.
items.cn: 名词以 -ure 构成，与 closure、exposure 同后缀。早期用法指揭示行为，随后出现“被揭示之事”的义项。

items.en: Securities law in the 1930s made disclosure a technical duty. Psychology and law later added self-disclosure and pre-trial disclosure as fixed terms.
items.cn: 1930 年代的证券法使 disclosure 成为一项技术性义务。心理学与法学随后加入 self-disclosure 与审判前开示等固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the container word and its opposite. The meaning group contrasts voluntary openness with leakage, revelation and announcement.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、容器类词与其反义方向；词义组把自愿公开与泄露、揭示、宣布区分开。

entries.definition: to make known or expose to view. The noun adds -ure to this verb.
entries.definitionCN: 使知晓或使显露。名词在其上加 -ure。

entries.definition: something enclosed, or the act of enclosing. It uses en- 'in' with the same claudere root, so it shuts in rather than opens out.
entries.definitionCN: 被围起之物，或围合行为。它用 en-“内”加同一 claudere 词根，因此是关进去而非打开。

entries.definition: the act of closing, or a sense of resolution. It is disclosure with the opening removed.
entries.definitionCN: 关闭行为，或一种了结感。它是去掉了“打开”的 disclosure。

entries.definition: a surprising fact made known, or divine disclosure. It stresses the impact of the news, while disclosure stresses the act and often a duty.
entries.definitionCN: 令人意外的事实被公布，或神的启示。它强调消息的冲击，而 disclosure 强调行为，常含义务。

entries.definition: the unauthorized release of information. A disclosure may be required by law; a leak never is.
entries.definitionCN: 未经授权的信息泄露。disclosure 可能是法律要求的；leak 从来不是。

entries.definition: a formal public statement. It is addressed outward to an audience, while disclosure is about removing concealment.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的公开声明。它朝外对受众说话，而 disclosure 关注的是去除掩盖。

entries.definition: the quality of operating openly. It is a standing condition, while a disclosure is a particular act.
entries.definitionCN: 公开运作的品质。它是持续状态，而 disclosure 是具体行为。

entries.definition: an admission of wrongdoing. It carries guilt, which disclosure does not necessarily carry.
entries.definitionCN: 对过错的承认。它带有罪感，而 disclosure 未必带有。

normalIntro.en: These hooks reduce the word to one physical act, un-shutting, and then locate who owns the closed thing in each sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词缩成一个物理动作——打开，然后在每个义项里找出那个被关着的东西归谁。

normal.en: See dis- + close: the shut thing is un-shut.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 close：被关上的东西被打开。

normal.en: Picture the wax seal breaking on the file. That crack is the disclosure.
normal.cn: 想象文件上的封蜡裂开。那道裂缝就是 disclosure。

normal.en: In finance, the drawer belongs to the company and the law says it must open.
normal.cn: 在金融里，抽屉属于公司，而法律说它必须打开。

normal.en: In psychology, the drawer is the self, and the person chooses when to open it.
normal.cn: 在心理学里，抽屉是自我，而本人选择何时打开。

normal.en: Contrast enclosure: en- shuts in, dis- lets out.
normal.cn: 对比 enclosure：en- 关进去，dis- 放出来。

abstract.en: Reduce every sense to two questions: what was closed, and who has the right to open it?
abstract.cn: 把每个义项缩成两个问题：什么被关着，谁有权打开？

abstract.en: Notice that disclosure changes relationships, not facts: the fact stays, the concealment ends.
abstract.cn: 注意披露改变的是关系而不是事实：事实不变，掩盖结束。

abstract.en: Keep the image of the seam: a disclosure is visible exactly at the line where covering meets content.
abstract.cn: 记住接缝的意象：披露恰恰在遮盖与内容相接的那条线上可见。

examples.en: The newspaper's disclosure forced the minister to resign.
examples.cn: 报纸的披露迫使部长辞职。

examples.en: Regulations require full disclosure of any conflict of interest.
examples.cn: 规定要求完全披露任何利益冲突。

examples.en: Too much self-disclosure too early can end a friendship.
examples.cn: 过早过多的自我表露可能终结一段友谊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯克罗热”：地里的斯克罗（disclose）被热得裂开，封口一开就全露出来——disclosure 就是披露。

root: 拉丁语 claudere“关闭”，加 dis- 构成“打开、揭示”的动词（拉丁少见，主要由罗曼语继承），经古法语 desclore 进入中古英语作 disclosen、disclose；加名词后缀 -ure 构成 disclosure。同根词有 include、exclude、conclude、clause、cloister。

sensesIntro.en: Disclosure is one physical gesture with many owners. A file is un-shut, a company's books are un-shut, a litigant's documents are un-shut, a self is un-shut, a government's records are un-shut. The nine senses differ in what was concealed and whether opening is voluntary, required or compulsory, but all of them turn concealment into visibility.
sensesIntro.cn: disclosure 是同一个物理动作，只是被打开的东西归属不同：文件被打开、公司账本被打开、诉讼方的文件被打开、自我被打开、政府记录被打开。九个义项的区别在于被掩盖的是什么，以及打开是自愿、应要求还是强制；但它们都把掩盖变成了可见。

core.en: Un-shutting: removing a cover so that the contents can be seen.
core.cn: 打开：移开遮盖，让内容被看见。

branches.en: GENERAL: the act of revealing, and the fact revealed.
branches.cn: 一般义：揭示行为，以及被揭示的事实。

branches.en: LAW AND BUSINESS: required publication and the documents that carry it.
branches.cn: 法律与商业：强制公布，以及承载它的文件。

branches.en: PSYCHOLOGY: opening the private self to another.
branches.cn: 心理学：把私密的自我向他人打开。

branches.en: ETHICS: declaring interests and hiding nothing relevant.
branches.cn: 伦理：声明利益，不隐瞒任何相关事项。

branches.en: GOVERNANCE: the state opening its records to citizens.
branches.cn: 治理：国家向公民打开记录。

intro.en: Disclosure is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb and a French noun suffix. The items follow claudere through English and show how the same root shuts, encloses and excludes.
intro.cn: disclosure 由拉丁前缀、拉丁动词与法语名词后缀组成。下列条目追踪 claudere 在英语中的走向，展示同一词根如何关闭、围住与排除。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the verb of shutting and its participle. They explain why 'close', 'clause' and 'cloister' all contain the same idea of an enclosed space.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“关闭”的动词及其分词。它们解释了为什么 close、clause、cloister 都含有同一个“围合空间”的观念。

items.meaning: the act of revealing; a revealed fact
items.meaningCN: 披露行为；被披露的事实
items.example: The disclosure ended the speculation.

items.meaning: to make known; to expose to view
items.example: He refused to disclose his sources.

items.meaning: the act of closing; a sense of ending
items.example: The talks reached a satisfying closure.
items.exampleCN: 会谈达成了令人满意的了结。

items.example: Please enclose a copy of the receipt.
The rules exclude part-time workers.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则把兼职人员排除在外。

items.meaning: to shut in; to contain as part
items.example: The price includes delivery.

items.meaning: to shut together; to bring to an end
items.example: The study concluded in June.

items.meaning: a closed unit of a sentence or document
items.example: Read the penalty clause carefully.

items.meaning: an enclosed religious walk or community
items.example: The monks walked in the cloister.

latinEntries.meaning: a shut place; a barrier, a cloister

definition_zh: 不连续；间断；断裂；不连贯之处
definition_en: a break or gap in something that would otherwise be continuous
core_image: 一条本该连着的线中间断了一截，两段对不上
scene: 地质剖面前，学生指着两块岩层之间一条突兀的界线。At the rock face the student points to a sharp line between two layers: there is no transition, only a discontinuity.
sceneCN: 这里 discontinuity 是「不连续、间断」（第 1、3 个义项：一般中断与地质不连续面）；句意：学生指着两层岩石间突兀的界线：这里没有过渡，只有一个间断。图中可辨识物件：岩层剖面、突兀的界线、地质锤、记录本。

pos.zh: 不连续；间断；断裂；不连贯之处

senses.title: A break in something continuous
senses.definition: a point or interval at which a continuous thing is interrupted
senses.definitionCN: 连续之物被打断的点或区间
senses.example: The narrative has a puzzling discontinuity in the middle.
senses.exampleCN: 叙述在中段有一处令人费解的断裂。
senses.why: Continuity is con- 'together' plus tenere 'to hold': parts holding together. Discontinuity is the failure of that hold, a place where the parts no longer meet.
senses.whyCN: continuity 是 con-“一起”加 tenere“握持”：各部分握在一起。discontinuity 就是这种握持失效，是各部分不再相接的地方。

senses.title: A jump in a series of values
senses.definition: a sudden change between successive values in a series, with no intermediate steps
senses.definitionCN: 序列中相邻值之间的突变，其间没有中间步骤
senses.example: The graph shows a sharp discontinuity at ten degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 图在十度处显示一个急剧的不连续。
senses.why: A continuous series can be traced without lifting the pen. A discontinuity is exactly where the pen must be lifted and placed somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 连续的序列可以一笔画到底。不连续正是必须把笔提起来、放到别处去的地方。

senses.title: A gap between rock layers
senses.definition: in geology, a boundary between rock layers that records a gap in deposition or a change in conditions
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中记录沉积间断或条件变化的岩层界线
senses.example: The Mohorovičić discontinuity separates crust from mantle.
senses.exampleCN: 莫霍不连续面分隔地壳与地幔。
senses.why: Rock normally accumulates layer on layer. A discontinuity marks the missing pages: time passed, but nothing was deposited, or everything older was eroded away.
senses.whyCN: 岩石通常一层压一层地堆积。不连续面标记的是缺失的书页：时间过去了，却没有沉积，或更早的一切都被侵蚀掉了。

senses.title: An abrupt change in a process
senses.definition: a sharp change in a trend, rate or condition rather than a smooth transition
senses.definitionCN: 趋势、速率或状况的急剧变化，而非平缓过渡
senses.example: The policy produced a discontinuity in migration patterns.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策造成迁徙模式的突变。
senses.why: Gradual change can be extrapolated; a discontinuity cannot. The word is used when the past no longer predicts the next point.
senses.whyCN: 渐变可以外推；不连续不能。当过去不再能预测下一个点时，人们就用这个词。

senses.title: A function that jumps
senses.definition: in mathematics, a point at which a function is not continuous, so its value or limit fails to match
senses.definitionCN: 数学中函数不连续的点，其函数值或极限无法衔接
senses.example: The function has a discontinuity where the denominator is zero.
senses.exampleCN: 该函数在分母为零处有一个间断点。
senses.why: Calculus defines continuity with limits: approaching from both sides must give the same value. A discontinuity is the point where the two approaches disagree.
senses.whyCN: 微积分用极限定义连续性：从两侧趋近必须得到同一个值。间断点就是两侧趋近不一致的地方。

senses.title: A rupture between historical periods
senses.definition: in history, a sharp break in institutions, beliefs or practices between periods
senses.definitionCN: 历史中两个时期之间制度、信仰或实践的急剧断裂
senses.example: Historians debate whether the fall of Rome was a discontinuity or a slow fade.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家争论罗马的衰亡是断裂还是缓慢消退。
senses.why: Periodisation needs seams. Calling a change a discontinuity asserts that the later period cannot be understood as a smooth continuation of the earlier one.
senses.whyCN: 分期需要接缝。把一次变化称为断裂，就是在断言后一时期不能被理解为前一时期的平滑延续。

senses.title: A cut between two shots
senses.definition: in film editing, a break in spatial or temporal continuity between shots
senses.definitionCN: 电影剪辑中镜头之间空间或时间连续性的中断
senses.example: The director used discontinuity to disorient the viewer.
senses.exampleCN: 导演用跳接让观众失去方向感。
senses.why: Classical editing hides its cuts so that space seems continuous. A deliberate discontinuity exposes the cut, and the exposure is the effect.
senses.whyCN: 古典剪辑隐藏剪切，使空间显得连续。刻意的跳接则暴露剪切，而这种暴露本身就是效果。

senses.title: A break in a tradition
senses.definition: the loss of transmission between generations, so that knowledge or practice is not passed on
senses.definitionCN: 代际传递的丧失，使知识或实践未能传下去
senses.example: Migration caused a discontinuity in the family's craft tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 迁徙造成这个家族手艺传统的断裂。
senses.why: A tradition is a chain of handing-over. When one link fails, the later generation starts again from nothing rather than from where the earlier one stopped.
senses.whyCN: 传统是一条递交的链条。某一环断了，后一代就从零开始，而不是从前一代停下的地方开始。

senses.title: A gap in a patient's care
senses.definition: in health care, an interruption in treatment or follow-up that leaves the patient without continuity of care
senses.definitionCN: 医疗中治疗或随访的中断，使病人失去连续照护
senses.example: The discontinuity between clinic and hospital led to a missed dose.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所与医院之间的衔接中断导致漏服一次药。
senses.why: Care is ideally a single thread held by one team. A discontinuity is where the thread drops, and the risk lies exactly at that drop.
senses.whyCN: 理想中的照护是由一支团队握着的单一线索。不连续就是线索掉落之处，而风险恰恰在那个落点。

intro.en: Discontinuity is dis- plus continuity, and continuity is Latin continuitas from continuus, from continere 'to hold together'. The word therefore means 'not holding together'. It is a learned formation, recorded in English from the 16th century.
intro.cn: discontinuity 是 dis- 加 continuity，而 continuity 是拉丁 continuitas，源于 continuus，再上溯 continere“握在一起”。因此这个词意为“没有握在一起”。它是学术性构造，16 世纪起见于英语。

items.en: The root *ten- meant 'to stretch, to hold'. It gives Latin tenere and English thin, tenant and the -tain of contain, retain and maintain.
items.cn: 词根 *ten- 意为“拉伸、握持”。它给出拉丁 tenere，以及英语 thin、tenant，和 contain、retain、maintain 中的 -tain。

items.en: Continere was com- 'together' plus tenere 'hold': to hold together, to contain. Its adjective continuus meant 'holding together without a gap', hence 'uninterrupted'.
items.cn: continere 是 com-“一起”加 tenere“握持”：握在一起、容纳。其形容词 continuus 意为“无缝隙地连在一起”，因而指“不间断的”。

items.en: The abstract noun continuitas named the state of being uninterrupted. Medieval and Renaissance Latin used it for both physical connection and logical sequence.
items.cn: 抽象名词 continuitas 指不中断的状态。中世纪与文艺复兴拉丁语用它兼指物理相连与逻辑连贯。

items.en: English continuity enters in the 16th century as 'uninterrupted connection'. The negative form discontinuity is coined soon after, on the Latin model rather than through French.
items.cn: 英语 continuity 于 16 世纪进入，意为“不中断的连接”。否定形式 discontinuity 随即仿拉丁语造出，而非经法语。

items.en: Calculus gives discontinuity its precise point-sense in the 17th and 18th centuries. Geology adopts it in the 19th for gaps in the rock record.
items.cn: 微积分在 17、18 世纪赋予 discontinuity 精确的“点”义。地质学在 19 世纪用它指岩石记录中的缺失。

items.en: History, film studies and anthropology extend the word to breaks in tradition, editing and care. The core meaning never changes: a place where a line that should hold does not.
items.cn: 历史学、电影研究与人类学把这个词扩展到传统、剪辑与照护中的中断。核心意义从未改变：本该握住的线没有握住的处所。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective, the adverb and the positive noun. The meaning group contrasts a structural gap with interruption, rupture and anomaly.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词、副词与肯定名词；词义组把结构性缺口与打断、破裂、异常区分开。

entries.definition: not continuous; broken by gaps. It describes the quality, while discontinuity names the gap itself.
entries.definitionCN: 不连续的；被间隙打断的。它描述性质，而 discontinuity 指间隙本身。

entries.definition: the state of being connected without a break. Add dis- and the holding fails.
entries.definitionCN: 无间断相连的状态。加上 dis-，握持就失效了。

entries.definition: the state of being next to or touching. It comes from tangere 'to touch', not from tenere, so it is not a true relative.
entries.definitionCN: 相邻或接触的状态。它来自 tangere“触摸”，而非 tenere，因此不是真正的同源词。

entries.definition: a break in an activity that may later resume. A discontinuity is structural; an interruption is often external and temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 活动中可能随后恢复的打断。discontinuity 是结构性的，interruption 常是外来的、暂时的。

entries.definition: a sudden breaking apart, as of relations or tissue. It is more forceful than discontinuity.
entries.definitionCN: 突然裂开，如关系或组织。它比 discontinuity 更有力。

entries.definition: an empty space between two things. It is the plain word; discontinuity is the technical framing of that gap.
entries.definitionCN: 两物之间的空处。它是普通词；discontinuity 是对这个空处的技术性表述。

entries.definition: something that departs from the expected pattern. It describes the odd item, while discontinuity describes the missing connection.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离预期模式的事物。它描述异常项，而 discontinuity 描述缺失的连接。

entries.definition: a gap or pause in something. It is the everyday equivalent and can be used in almost every sense here.
entries.definitionCN: 事物中的缺口或停顿。它是日常对应词，几乎可用于此处每个义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks hold the word against its positive twin, then walk the single image of a broken line through graphs, rocks, history and care.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词与它的肯定双胞胎对着记，再把“断线”这一个意象走过图表、岩层、历史与照护。

normal.en: See the pair: continuity holds together, discontinuity fails to hold.
normal.cn: 看见这一对：continuity 握在一起，discontinuity 没握住。

normal.en: Picture a pencil line with a jump in it: the jump is the discontinuity.
normal.cn: 想象一条中间跳开的铅笔线：那一跳就是 discontinuity。

normal.en: In geology, the missing layers are missing pages, not torn ones.
normal.cn: 在地质里，缺失的岩层是缺页，而不是被撕掉的页。

normal.en: In maths, discontinuity is where the two approaches to the point disagree.
normal.cn: 在数学里，不连续就是两侧趋近该点却意见不一致的地方。

normal.en: In film, a deliberate jump cut exposes the seam that classical editing hides.
normal.cn: 在电影里，刻意的跳接暴露了古典剪辑所隐藏的接缝。

abstract.en: Reduce every sense to one question: where should the line have continued, and why did it not?
abstract.cn: 把每个义项缩成一个问题：线本该在哪里继续，为什么没有？

abstract.en: Notice that discontinuity is defined by expectation: a gap only counts as one if continuity was expected.
abstract.cn: 注意不连续是由预期定义的：只有本来期待连续时，缺口才算不连续。

abstract.en: Hold the seam image: every sense marks a place where two sides fail to meet.
abstract.cn: 记住接缝意象：每个义项都标记一个两侧未能相接的地方。

examples.en: The data show a clear discontinuity around 1990.
examples.cn: 数据在 1990 年前后显示出明显的不连续。

examples.en: The boundary between the two rock types is a major geological discontinuity.
examples.cn: 两种岩石之间的界线是一个重要的地质不连续面。

examples.en: War created a discontinuity in the country's literary tradition.
examples.cn: 战争在该国的文学传统中造成了断裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯空提牛厄地”：地斯空提的那头牛（discontinuity）走到半路断了绳子，绳子一断就不连续了。

root: 拉丁语 continere“握在一起”（com- 一起 + tenere 握持），形容词 continuus“无缝隙相连的”，抽象名词 continuitas“连续性”；加否定前缀 dis- 构成 discontinuity。注意 contiguity 来自 tangere“触摸”，不是同源词。

sensesIntro.en: Discontinuity is a negative noun: it exists only where continuity was expected. A story has a seam, a graph has a jump, a rock record has missing pages, a history has a rupture, a film has a visible cut, a family has a broken chain of handing-over, a patient has a dropped thread of care. The nine senses differ in the material, but all mark the same thing: a place where two sides that should meet do not.
sensesIntro.cn: discontinuity 是一个否定性名词：只有在本该连续的地方，它才存在。故事有接缝，图表有跳变，岩石记录有缺页，历史有断裂，电影有可见的剪切，家族有断掉的传递链，病人有掉落的照护线索。九个义项材料不同，但标记的是同一件事：两边本该相接却没有相接的地方。

core.en: A failed hold: the place where a continuous line breaks.
core.cn: 握持失效：连续之线断开的地方。

branches.en: FORM: a break in narrative, a jump in values, a point where limits disagree.
branches.cn: 形式：叙述的断裂、数值的跳变、极限不一致的点。

branches.en: EARTH: missing layers in the rock record.
branches.cn: 大地：岩石记录中缺失的层。

branches.en: TIME: abrupt change in processes and between historical periods.
branches.cn: 时间：过程与历史时期之间的突变。

branches.en: FILM: a cut that refuses to be hidden.
branches.cn: 电影：拒绝被隐藏的剪切。

branches.en: HUMAN CHAINS: broken tradition, interrupted care.
branches.cn: 人的链条：断掉的传统、被打断的照护。

intro.en: Discontinuity is dis- plus continuity, itself continere plus -itas. The items show the tenere family, where the same 'hold' root appears in contain, retain and maintain.
intro.cn: discontinuity 是 dis- 加 continuity，而 continuity 是 continere 加 -itas。下列条目展示 tenere 词族，同一个“握持”词根出现在 contain、retain、maintain 中。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb of holding together, its adjective and its abstract noun. They make clear why continuity is about holding, not about touching.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“握在一起”的动词、形容词与抽象名词。它们说明 continuity 关乎握持，而非触摸。

items.example: There is a discontinuity in the record.
The film values continuity of action.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片重视动作的连贯。

items.example: The process is discontinuous, in stages.
items.exampleCN: 这个过程是分阶段的、不连续的。

items.example: A continuous line runs across the page.
items.exampleCN: 一条不断的线贯穿页面。

items.example: The rain continued all night.

items.meaning: to hold together; to have within
items.example: The box contains old photographs.
The soil retains moisture well.

items.meaning: to hold in the hand; to keep up
items.example: They maintain the old bridge.

items.meaning: one who holds land or property
items.example: The tenant renewed the lease.

definition_zh: 发现；被发现的事物；探索；（法律）证据开示
definition_en: the act of finding something that was previously unknown or hidden, or the thing so found
core_image: 揭开幕布，后面是一个此前没人知道存在的洞口
scene: 洞穴口，考察队把覆盖的藤蔓拨开，露出一个从未被记录的入口。At the cave mouth the team parts the vines and finds an entrance no record mentions: a discovery.
sceneCN: 这里 discovery 是「发现」（第 1、2、4 个义项：发现行为与被发现之物）；句意：考察队拨开藤蔓，露出一个从未被记录的入口，这是一次发现。图中可辨识物件：藤蔓、洞口、头灯、测绘板。

pos.zh: 发现；被发现的事物；（法律）证据开示

derivatives.zh: 盖子；覆盖（dis- 去掉的正是它）
覆盖范围；报道（同词根，不同方向）

senses.title: Finding what was hidden
senses.definition: the act of coming upon something that was unknown, concealed or unsuspected
senses.definitionCN: 遇到此前未知、被掩藏或未被想到之物的行为
senses.example: The discovery of the tunnel explained the noises.
senses.exampleCN: 这条隧道的发现解释了那些声响。
senses.why: Latin cooperire is com- 'together' plus operire 'to cover'. Discover is to take that cover off, so the act is literally an uncovering rather than an inventing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 cooperire 是 com-“一起”加 operire“覆盖”。discover 就是把那层覆盖拿掉，因此这个行为字面上是“揭开”，而不是“发明”。

senses.title: The thing that was found
senses.definition: an object, place or fact that has been found and is now known
senses.definitionCN: 已被找到并为人所知的对象、地点或事实
senses.example: The museum put its latest discoveries on display.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出了最新的发现物。
senses.why: As with disclosure, the process noun also names its product. A discovery can be an event in a laboratory or an object in a case.
senses.whyCN: 与 disclosure 一样，过程名词也指称其产物。discovery 可以是实验室里的一次事件，也可以是展柜里的一件东西。

senses.title: A finding in science
senses.definition: a new fact, effect or phenomenon established by observation or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察或实验确立的新事实、效应或现象
senses.example: The discovery of the particle required a larger accelerator.
senses.exampleCN: 这个粒子的发现需要更大的加速器。
senses.why: Science distinguishes finding what exists from inventing a device. Discovery claims that the thing was there before anyone looked, which is why priority disputes matter.
senses.whyCN: 科学区分“找到已存在的东西”与“发明装置”。discovery 声称那东西在有人看之前就在那里，这正是优先权之争如此重要的原因。

senses.title: Reaching a place no outsider knew
senses.definition: the first arrival of an outside group at a place unknown to them
senses.definitionCN: 外来群体首次抵达一个对他们而言未知的地方
senses.example: The Age of Discovery reshaped world trade.
senses.exampleCN: 大发现时代重塑了世界贸易。
senses.why: The word is written from the outsider's side: the place already had inhabitants, but not in the outsider's knowledge. This is why historians now mark its bias.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是从外来者一侧写的：那地方本有居民，只是不在外来者的知识里。正因如此，历史学家现在会标注这种偏向。

senses.title: Evidence revealed before trial
senses.definition: in law, the pre-trial procedure by which each side obtains the other's documents and evidence
senses.definitionCN: 法律中审判前双方获取对方文件与证据的程序
senses.example: Discovery produced thousands of pages of emails.
senses.exampleCN: 证据开示产生了数千页电子邮件。
senses.why: The cover here is procedural secrecy. Discovery removes it so that neither side can surprise the other at trial. The same Latin image serves a courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 这里的覆盖是程序上的保密。discovery 把它揭开，使双方无法在审判时突袭对方。同一个拉丁意象被用到了法庭。

senses.title: Learning something about oneself
senses.definition: the realization of a personal truth about one's own abilities, desires or identity
senses.definitionCN: 对自身能力、愿望或身份之真相的领悟
senses.example: Travel became a journey of self-discovery.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行成了一段自我发现之旅。
senses.why: What was covered is not a place but one's own interior. The metaphor treats the self as terrain that can be explored.
senses.whyCN: 被覆盖的不是地点，而是自己的内部。这个比喻把自我当作可以勘探的地形。

senses.title: Finding a useful substance or drug
senses.titleCN: 有用物质或药物的发现
senses.definition: the identification of a substance, organism or compound with practical value
senses.definitionCN: 对具有实用价值的物质、生物或化合物的确认
senses.example: The discovery of penicillin changed medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 青霉素的发现改变了医学。
senses.why: The mould existed long before anyone noticed its effect. Discovery names the moment the effect entered human use, not the moment the mould began.
senses.whyCN: 霉菌早在有人注意到它的作用之前就存在。discovery 命名的是这种作用进入人类使用的那一刻，而不是霉菌开始存在的那一刻。

senses.title: Finding something while looking elsewhere
senses.definition: an unexpected finding made while pursuing a different aim, often called serendipity
senses.definitionCN: 在追求另一目标时意外获得的发现，常称 serendipity
senses.example: The adhesive was a chance discovery.
senses.exampleCN: 这种黏合剂是一次偶然发现。
senses.why: The cover comes off by accident. The word still marks the uncovering, but the intention that usually precedes it is absent.
senses.whyCN: 覆盖是偶然掉落的。这个词仍标记“揭开”，但通常先于它的意图缺席了。

senses.title: Learning by finding things out
senses.definition: in education, an approach in which learners find principles for themselves rather than being told them
senses.definitionCN: 教育中让学习者自己找出原理而非被告知的方法
senses.example: Discovery learning works best with guided tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 发现式学习在有引导的任务中效果最好。
senses.why: The student is placed in the position of the explorer. What the teacher withholds is the cover, and the lesson is the act of removing it.
senses.whyCN: 学生被放在探索者的位置。教师扣下的就是那层覆盖，而课程正是揭开它的动作。

intro.en: Discovery is dis- plus cover plus -y. Cover comes from Old French covrir, from Latin cooperire, com- 'together' plus operire 'to cover'. Discover therefore means 'to un-cover', and the noun follows the verb.
intro.cn: discovery 是 dis- 加 cover 再加 -y。cover 来自古法语 covrir，上溯拉丁 cooperire，即 com-“一起”加 operire“覆盖”。因此 discover 意为“揭开”，名词随动词而来。

items.en: Operire meant 'to cover, to shut in'. With com- it became cooperire, 'to cover completely'. The root also gives operculum, a lid.
items.cn: operire 意为“覆盖、封闭”。加 com- 成为 cooperire“完全覆盖”。同一词根还给出 operculum“盖子”。

items.en: Old French covrir reduced the Latin verb to a single syllable. English cover comes from it, and so does the whole family of covering words.
items.cn: 古法语 covrir 把这个拉丁动词压缩成一个音节。英语 cover 由此而来，整套“覆盖”词族也随之而来。

items.en: Old French descovrir meant 'to uncover, to reveal'. It passed into Middle English as discover, first in the literal sense of removing a covering.
items.cn: 古法语 descovrir 意为“揭开、显露”。它进入中古英语作 discover，最初就是字面上移开覆盖物。

items.en: With ocean voyages, discover shifted to 'reach a place previously unknown to us'. The word travels with the explorer, not with the place.
items.cn: 随着远洋航行，discover 转向“抵达一个我们此前未知的地方”。这个词跟着探索者走，而不是跟着地方走。

items.en: The noun appears with -y, modelled on French descouverte. It covers both the act and the thing found, a pattern English keeps in finding and invention.
items.cn: 名词以 -y 出现，仿法语 descouverte。它兼指行为与所发现之物，英语在 finding 与 invention 中也保留这一模式。

items.en: Legal discovery becomes a fixed procedure in English-speaking courts, and discovery learning enters education theory through Bruner in the 1960s.
items.cn: 法律上的证据开示在英语法庭成为固定程序；发现式学习则经布鲁纳在 1960 年代进入教育理论。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the person and the cover that the prefix removes. The meaning group contrasts finding with inventing, detecting and exploring.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、指人名词，以及被前缀移开的“覆盖”；词义组把“发现”与“发明”“检测”“探索”区分开。

entries.definition: to find something hidden or unknown. The noun adds -y.
entries.definitionCN: 找到隐藏或未知之物。名词加 -y。

entries.definition: the person who makes a discovery. It names the agent, while discovery names the event.
entries.definitionCN: 作出发现的人。它指施动者，而 discovery 指事件。

entries.definition: the extent to which something is covered, or news reporting. It comes from cover, so it adds a cover rather than removing one.
entries.definitionCN: 被覆盖的范围，或新闻报道。它来自 cover，因此是加上覆盖而非移开。

entries.definition: the creation of something that did not exist before. Discovery finds what was already there; invention brings it into being.
entries.definitionCN: 创造此前不存在的东西。discovery 找到本已存在之物；invention 使之产生。

entries.definition: the act of noticing that something is present, often with an instrument. It is narrower than discovery and need not involve anything unknown.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉某物存在，常借助仪器。它比 discovery 窄，且不必涉及未知之物。

entries.definition: the activity of travelling or investigating to learn what is there. It is the process that may lead to a discovery.
entries.definitionCN: 为弄清有什么而旅行或调查的活动。它是可能导致发现的过程。

entries.definition: a sudden important advance. It stresses the change that follows, while discovery stresses the finding itself.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的重要进展。它强调随之而来的改变，而 discovery 强调找到本身。

entries.definition: a result or conclusion reached by research. It is the technical word in reports, while discovery is the public word.
entries.definitionCN: 研究得出的结果或结论。它是报告中的技术用词，而 discovery 是公众用词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks reduce the word to one gesture, taking a cover off, then vary who owned the cover: ground, secrecy, self, ignorance.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词缩成一个动作——把覆盖拿掉，再变化那层覆盖归谁：土地、保密、自我、无知。

normal.en: See dis- + cover: the cover is removed. Nothing is created.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 cover：覆盖被移开。没有东西被创造。

normal.en: Picture vines pulled back from a cave mouth. The cave was always there.
normal.cn: 想象藤蔓从洞口被拨开。洞一直在那里。

normal.en: For science, ask what existed before anyone looked: that is what was discovered.
normal.cn: 科学方面问：在有人看之前什么已经存在？那就是被发现的。

normal.en: In law, the cover is secrecy, and discovery is the rule that lifts it.
normal.cn: 法律里，覆盖是保密，discovery 是揭开它的规则。

normal.en: For self-discovery, the terrain is your own interior, not a map.
normal.cn: 自我发现里，地形是你自己的内部，而不是一张地图。

abstract.en: Reduce every sense to one test: was it there before, and did someone finally remove the cover?
abstract.cn: 把每个义项缩成一个检验：它本来就在吗，有人终于把覆盖移开了吗？

abstract.en: Notice the word's bias: it records the moment of knowing, not the moment of existing.
abstract.cn: 注意这个词的偏向：它记录的是知道的那一刻，而不是存在的那一刻。

abstract.en: Keep discovery and invention apart by asking whether the thing could have existed without us.
abstract.cn: 用“那东西能否不依赖我们而存在”来分开 discovery 与 invention。

examples.en: The discovery of the wreck solved a century-old mystery.
examples.cn: 沉船的发现解开了一个百年之谜。

examples.en: Her discoveries in genetics earned international recognition.
examples.cn: 她在遗传学上的发现赢得了国际认可。

examples.en: The court allowed limited discovery of the internal emails.
examples.cn: 法院允许对内部邮件进行有限的证据开示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯柯沃瑞”：地斯柯（discover）在沃瑞（very）那边掀开盖子，一掀就看见——discovery 就是发现。

root: 拉丁语 operire“覆盖”，加 com- 成 cooperire“完全覆盖”，经古法语 covrir 进入英语作 cover；加否定前缀 des-/dis- 成 descovrir、discover“揭开”，再以 -y 构成名词 discovery。同根词有 cover、coverage、operculum。

sensesIntro.en: Discovery is a cover being removed. What lies under it changes from sense to sense: a cave, a fact, a particle, a continent, a hidden email, one's own desire, a mould with an effect, an accident, a principle a pupil works out alone. In every case the thing was already there; the event is the moment the cover comes off and it enters knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: discovery 是一层覆盖被移开。覆盖下面的东西逐义变化：洞穴、事实、粒子、大陆、隐藏的邮件、自己的愿望、有效用的霉菌、一次意外、学生独自算出的原理。每一种情况下，那东西本来就在；事件是覆盖被揭开、它进入知识的那一刻。

core.en: Un-covering: taking a cover off something that was already there.
core.cn: 揭开：把覆盖从本已存在之物上拿掉。

branches.en: GENERAL: the act of uncovering and the thing uncovered.
branches.cn: 一般义：揭开的行为与被揭开之物。

branches.en: SCIENCE: established facts, useful substances and lucky finds.
branches.cn: 科学：确立的事实、有用的物质与幸运的发现。

branches.en: GEOGRAPHY: first arrival, told from the outsider's side.
branches.cn: 地理：首次抵达，以外来者的视角叙述。

branches.en: LAW: procedural secrecy lifted before trial.
branches.cn: 法律：审判前揭开的程序保密。

branches.en: PERSON: exploring the self, and learning by finding out.
branches.cn: 个人：探索自我，以及通过自己找出而学习。

intro.en: Discovery is dis- plus cover plus -y. The items show that cover and its family all point the opposite way, and that the prefix carries the whole idea of reversal.
intro.cn: discovery 是 dis- 加 cover 再加 -y。下列条目展示 cover 及其词族都朝相反方向，并展示这个前缀承载了整个反转的意思。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are the covering verb and its compound. They show that English has two layers from the same source: the everyday cover and the technical operculum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“覆盖”的动词及其复合形式。它们说明英语从同一来源得到两层词：日常的 cover 与术语 operculum。

items.meaning: the act of finding out; the thing found
items.example: The discovery changed the field.
items.exampleCN: 这一发现改变了这个领域。

items.example: They discovered a new species.
items.exampleCN: 他们发现了一个新物种。

items.meaning: to place something over; a lid
items.example: Cover the pot and lower the heat.
The network has wide coverage.

items.meaning: to remove a cover; to expose
items.example: They uncovered the old foundation.

items.meaning: to get back; to return to health
items.example: He recovered within a week.
She disclosed the terms.
The sensor detects smoke.
The fish closes its operculum.

definition_zh: 歧视；辨别；辨别力；（心理）辨别学习；区别对待
definition_en: unfair treatment based on a category, or the ability to perceive fine differences
core_image: 一把细齿筛子：同样的沙子，细齿能把大小不同的颗粒分开
scene: 实验室里，技术员用一套细筛把沙样分成几层，墙上还贴着一张写有平等待遇的告示。The technician separates a sand sample into layers with a set of sieves, while a notice on the wall demands equal treatment: both are called discrimination.
sceneCN: 这里 discrimination 是「辨别」与「歧视」（第 1、2 个义项：歧视与辨别力）；句意：技术员用细筛把沙样分层，墙上告示要求平等待遇；这两件事都叫 discrimination。图中可辨识物件：套筛、分层沙样、告示、记录表。

collocations.zh: A 与 B 之间的区分

forms.label: 复数（多种歧视或辨别行为）

senses.title: Treating people unequally by category
senses.titleCN: 按类别不平等对待（歧视）
senses.definition: the unjust or prejudicial treatment of people because of their group, such as race, sex, age or disability
senses.definitionCN: 因种族、性别、年龄或残障等群体归属而对人作出的不公正或有偏见的对待
senses.example: The law prohibits discrimination in hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止在招聘中歧视。
senses.why: Latin discriminare meant 'to separate, to set apart'. The modern social sense keeps the separating but drops the justification: people are sorted by category rather than by merit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 discriminare 意为“分开、区分”。现代的社会义保留了“分开”，却抽掉了正当理由：人被按类别分类，而不是按能力。

senses.title: Seeing fine differences
senses.definition: the ability to perceive and state small differences between things that are alike
senses.definitionCN: 觉察并说明相似事物之间细微差别的能力
senses.example: A good translator needs fine discrimination between near-synonyms.
senses.exampleCN: 好的译者需要对近义词的精细辨别力。
senses.why: Discrimen was the dividing line between things. To discriminate is to see where that line falls, and the noun names the skill of seeing it.
senses.whyCN: discrimen 是事物之间的分界线。to discriminate 就是看出那条线落在哪里，名词就指这种看线的本领。

senses.title: Telling stimuli apart
senses.definition: in perception, the detection of a difference between two stimuli, such as two tones or two shades
senses.definitionCN: 知觉中对两个刺激之间差异的觉察，如两个音或两种色调
senses.example: Colour discrimination declines with age.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色辨别力随年龄下降。
senses.why: The laboratory version strips the word of moral content. Here discrimination is a threshold: how small a difference can still be detected.
senses.whyCN: 实验室版本剥去了道德内容。这里的 discrimination 是一个阈值：多小的差别仍能被察觉。

senses.title: Learning which cue predicts what
senses.definition: in psychology, the learning of a response to one stimulus and the withholding of it from another
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中对一个刺激作出反应、对另一个刺激不作反应的学习
senses.example: Discrimination learning separates the rewarded tone from the unrewarded one.
senses.exampleCN: 辨别学习把有奖励的音与无奖励的音分开。
senses.why: An organism that responds to everything cannot learn. Discrimination is the narrowing of response to the cue that actually predicts the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 对一切都反应的生物无法学习。辨别就是把反应收窄到真正预示结果的线索上。

senses.title: Sorting by group averages
senses.definition: in economics, treating an individual according to the average traits of their group rather than their own
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中按群体平均特征而非个人特征对待个体
senses.example: Statistical discrimination can persist even without prejudice.
senses.exampleCN: 即使没有偏见，统计性歧视也可能持续。
senses.why: The word separates the mechanism from the motive. Using group averages is a form of separating, and it can be economically rational while still being unjust.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把机制与动机分开。使用群体平均是一种分类，它可能在经济上理性，却仍然不公。

senses.title: The legal prohibition of bias
senses.definition: in law, the body of rules that forbids unequal treatment on protected grounds
senses.definitionCN: 法律中禁止基于受保护理由不平等对待的规则体系
senses.example: Discrimination law covers both direct and indirect bias.
senses.exampleCN: 反歧视法涵盖直接与间接偏见。
senses.why: Here the noun names the target of regulation rather than the act. A discrimination claim asserts that the separating was unjust and therefore actionable.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词指监管的对象，而不是行为本身。一项歧视主张断言那次区分不公正，因而可诉。

senses.title: Distinguishing between diagnoses
senses.definition: in medicine, the process of distinguishing between conditions that present similar signs
senses.definitionCN: 医学中区分表现相似体征的多种病症的过程
senses.example: Careful discrimination between the two fevers is essential.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细鉴别这两种发热至关重要。
senses.why: Clinical work depends on discriminatio, the Latin word for a distinguishing. The skill is to place each case on the correct side of a line.
senses.whyCN: 临床工作依赖 discriminatio，即拉丁语的“分辨”。这项本领就是把每个病例放到分界线的正确一侧。

senses.title: Separating one signal from noise
senses.definition: in engineering, the separation of a wanted signal from background noise or from other signals
senses.definitionCN: 工程中把所需信号从背景噪声或其他信号中分离出来
senses.example: The receiver's discrimination is limited by thermal noise.
senses.exampleCN: 接收机的鉴别能力受热噪声限制。
senses.why: The sieve image returns literally: a receiver passes what matches and rejects what does not. Here discrimination is a technical measure of selectivity.
senses.whyCN: 筛子意象在这里字面回归：接收机通过匹配的，拒绝不匹配的。这里的 discrimination 是选择性的技术度量。

senses.title: Favouring a disadvantaged group
senses.definition: in policy, the deliberate favouring of a disadvantaged group to correct past imbalance, often called positive discrimination
senses.definitionCN: 政策中为纠正过往失衡而刻意优待弱势群体，常称正向歧视
senses.example: Positive discrimination is lawful only within narrow limits.
senses.exampleCN: 正向歧视只在狭窄范围内合法。
senses.why: The word is turned inside out: the same sorting mechanism is used to undo earlier sorting. The adjective, not the noun, carries the moral verdict.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被翻了个面：同一个分类机制被用来抵消早先的分类。道德判断由形容词承担，而不是名词。

intro.en: Discrimination is Latin discriminare plus -ion. Discriminare comes from discrimen 'a dividing line', from discernere, dis- 'apart' plus cernere 'to sift, to separate'. The word begins as a neutral act of sorting and only later acquires its social accusation.
intro.cn: discrimination 是拉丁 discriminare 加 -ion。discriminare 来自 discrimen“分界线”，再上溯 discernere，即 dis-“分开”加 cernere“筛、分离”。这个词起初是中性的分类行为，后来才获得社会指控的色彩。

items.en: The root *krei- meant 'to sieve, to separate'. It gives Latin cernere and Greek krinein, from which crisis and critic descend.
items.cn: 词根 *krei- 意为“筛、分离”。它给出拉丁 cernere 与希腊 krinein，后者衍生出 crisis 与 critic。

items.en: Cernere meant 'to sift, to distinguish'. With dis- it became discernere, 'to separate out, to perceive a difference'. English discern comes straight from it.
items.cn: cernere 意为“筛、分辨”。加 dis- 成为 discernere“分开、看出差别”。英语 discern 直接由此而来。

items.en: Discrimen named a dividing line, a decisive moment, and later a risk. Discriminare meant 'to divide, to distinguish', still neutral in classical use.
items.cn: discrimen 指分界线、决定性时刻，后也指风险。discriminare 意为“分开、区分”，在古典用法中仍是中性的。

items.en: English discrimination first means 'distinction, discernment'. The sense of 'unfair treatment' appears in the 19th century, when social categories become grounds for exclusion.
items.cn: 英语 discrimination 最初意为“区分、识别力”。“不公平对待”的义项在 19 世纪出现，当时社会类别成为排斥的理由。

items.en: Anti-discrimination law in the 20th century makes the negative sense dominant. Positive discrimination is coined later as a deliberate exception.
items.cn: 20 世纪的反歧视法使负面义占主导。positive discrimination 后来被造出，作为刻意的例外。

items.en: Psychology, economics and engineering keep the neutral sense alive: stimulus discrimination, statistical discrimination, signal discrimination.
items.cn: 心理学、经济学与工程学让中性义继续存活：刺激辨别、统计性歧视、信号鉴别。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the negative adjective and its opposite. The meaning group contrasts unfair sorting with legitimate distinction and with other forms of prejudice.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、负面形容词与其反义词；词义组把不公平分类与正当区分及其他形式的偏见对照。

entries.definition: to distinguish, or to treat unfairly by category. It carries both senses of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 区分，或按类别不公平对待。它兼有名词的两个义项。

entries.definition: showing unfair treatment by category. It takes the moral verdict that the noun alone does not.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出按类别不公平对待的。它承担了名词本身没有的道德判断。

entries.definition: done without distinguishing, as indiscriminate bombing. It means no line is drawn at all.
entries.definitionCN: 不加区分的，如无差别轰炸。它指根本不划线。

entries.definition: a difference properly recognized, or a mark of excellence. It is the neutral relative of sense 02.
entries.definitionCN: 被恰当认识到的差别，或优异的标志。它是第 2 义项的中性亲属。

entries.definition: a preconceived opinion not based on facts. Prejudice is the attitude; discrimination is the treatment that may follow.
entries.definitionCN: 不基于事实的成见。prejudice 是态度，discrimination 是可能随后的对待。

entries.definition: the process of becoming or making different. It describes divergence, not unequal treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 变得或使变得不同的过程。它描述分化，而非不平等对待。

entries.definition: a leaning that distorts judgement. A bias may stay in the mind; discrimination is its visible application.
entries.definitionCN: 使判断偏斜的倾向。偏见可以只停留在心里；discrimination 是其可见的施行。

entries.definition: the enforced separation of groups. It is one institutional form that discrimination can take.
entries.definitionCN: 对群体的强制隔离。它是 discrimination 可能采取的一种制度形式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the sieve image in front, then show how the same sorting becomes a skill, a laboratory threshold and an injustice.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把筛子意象放在最前面，再展示同一种分类如何成为本领、实验室阈值与不公。

normal.en: See cernere, 'to sift': discrimination is sorting with a sieve.
normal.cn: 看见 cernere“筛”：discrimination 就是拿筛子分类。

normal.en: For the skill sense, admire a translator who can sift two near-synonyms.
normal.cn: 本领义方面，想象一位能把两个近义词筛开的译者。

normal.en: For the legal sense, notice the sieve is applied to people, and that is the problem.
normal.cn: 法律义方面，注意筛子被用到了人身上，问题就在这里。

normal.en: Keep the pair prejudice and discrimination: the attitude and the act.
normal.cn: 记住 prejudice 与 discrimination 这一对：态度与行为。

normal.en: Remember positive discrimination turns the sieve around to undo old sorting.
normal.cn: 记住 positive discrimination 把筛子翻过来，用来抵消旧的分类。

abstract.en: Reduce both poles to one operation: drawing a line. Whether it is just depends on what the line is drawn on.
abstract.cn: 把两端缩成一个操作：划线。它是否公正，取决于线画在什么之上。

abstract.en: Notice that the neutral and the accused senses use the same mechanism; only the justification differs.
abstract.cn: 注意中性义与受指责义使用同一机制；差别只在正当理由。

abstract.en: Ask of every use: is the difference being perceived, or is it being imposed?
abstract.cn: 对每个用法都问：这个差别是被察觉到的，还是被强加上去的？

examples.en: The study found discrimination against older applicants.
examples.cn: 这项研究发现对年长申请者的歧视。

examples.en: Good taste depends on discrimination between the merely loud and the truly strong.
examples.cn: 好的品味取决于能否分辨仅仅响亮与真正有力。

examples.en: The filter's discrimination between the two signals is excellent.
examples.cn: 该滤波器对两种信号的鉴别非常出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯克利米内申”：地斯克利（discreet）在米内（mini）筛子里挑米，挑得细就是辨别，挑得偏就成了歧视。

root: 拉丁语 cernere“筛、分辨”，加 dis- 成 discernere“分开、辨别”，其名词 discrimen“分界线”再派生动词 discriminare“区分”；加 -ion 构成 discrimination。同根词有 discern、discernment、certain、secret、crisis（希腊 krinein 同源）。

sensesIntro.en: Discrimination is one operation seen from two moral sides. The operation is drawing a line: between two shades, two tones, two diagnoses, two signals, two groups of people. In the laboratory and the clinic this is a skill; in the labour market and the law it becomes an accusation. The nine senses keep the same sieve and change what is being sifted and whether the sifting was justified.
sensesIntro.cn: discrimination 是同一个操作的两个道德侧面。这个操作就是划线：在两种色调、两个音、两个诊断、两个信号、两群人之间划线。在实验室与诊室里这是本领；在劳动力市场与法律里，它变成指控。九个义项用同一把筛子，只改变筛的是什么、以及筛得是否正当。

core.en: Drawing a line: separating things, or separating people.
core.cn: 划线：把事物分开，或把人分开。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND LAW: unfair sorting, its prohibition, and its deliberate reversal.
branches.cn: 社会与法律：不公分类、对它的禁止，以及刻意的反转。

branches.en: PERCEPTION AND CLINIC: fine distinctions between similar things.
branches.cn: 知觉与临床：相似事物之间的精细区分。

branches.en: SENSES: the threshold at which a difference is noticed.
branches.cn: 感官：差别被察觉的阈值。

branches.en: LEARNING: responding to one cue and not another.
branches.cn: 学习：对某个线索反应，对另一个不反应。

branches.en: STATISTICS AND ENGINEERING: group averages and signal selectivity.
branches.cn: 统计与工程：群体平均值与信号选择性。

intro.en: Discrimination ends in -ion on a Latin verb. The items follow cernere through discern, certain and secret, and show the two adjectives that carry opposite moral verdicts.
intro.cn: discrimination 是拉丁动词加 -ion。下列条目追踪 cernere 在 discern、certain、secret 中的走向，并展示两个承担相反道德判断的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries move from the verb of sifting to the line it draws and the act of drawing it. The metaphor of a boundary is present at every step.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目从“筛”的动词走到它画出的线，再到画线的行为。边界的比喻在每一步都在。

items.meaning: unfair treatment; the power to distinguish
items.example: Discrimination on grounds of age is illegal.
items.exampleCN: 基于年龄的歧视是非法的。

items.example: The test discriminates between weak and strong readers.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试能区分阅读强弱。

items.example: The policy was ruled discriminatory.
items.exampleCN: 该政策被裁定为歧视性。

items.example: The attack was indiscriminate.
She has a discriminating palate.
I could barely discern the outline.
She made a discreet inquiry.
The outcome is certain.
They kept the plan secret.

latinEntries.meaning: to sift, to separate, to distinguish
to separate out; to perceive a difference
a dividing line; a decisive moment

definition_zh: 讨论；商议；论述；（论文的）讨论部分
definition_en: a conversation or exchange of views about a subject, or a written treatment of it
core_image: 几个人围着一张桌子，把一个问题反复翻面看
scene: 研讨室里，四个人围着一张圆桌，把一份报告推来推去，边指边辩。Four people around a round table push a report back and forth and argue over it: an intense discussion.
sceneCN: 这里 discussion 是「讨论」（第 1、2 个义项：交谈与研讨）；句意：四个人围着圆桌把报告推来推去、边指边辩，这是一场激烈的讨论。图中可辨识物件：圆桌、报告、白板、四把椅子。

pos.zh: 讨论；商议；论述；讨论部分

derivatives.zh: 脑震荡（同词根，不同前缀）
打击乐；撞击（同词根，不同前缀）

senses.title: Talking a subject over
senses.definition: a conversation in which people exchange views about a subject
senses.definitionCN: 人们就某话题交换看法的交谈
senses.example: We had a long discussion about the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 我们就预算进行了长时间的讨论。
senses.why: Latin discutere is dis- 'apart' plus quatere 'to shake'. A discussion shakes a subject apart to see what is inside it, and the noun names that joint shaking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 discutere 是 dis-“分开”加 quatere“摇动”。讨论把话题摇散，看看里面有什么，名词命名这种共同的摇动。

senses.title: Formal debate among experts
senses.definition: a structured exchange of arguments, as at a conference or in a seminar
senses.definitionCN: 在会议或研讨班上进行的结构化论点交换
senses.example: The conference ended with a discussion on climate policy.
senses.exampleCN: 会议以一场关于气候政策的讨论结束。
senses.why: The shaking becomes orderly: each speaker turns the topic to a new face. The word marks the format rather than the friendship of the participants.
senses.whyCN: 这种摇动变得有秩序：每位发言者把话题翻到一个新面。这个词标记的是形式，而不是参与者之间的亲疏。

senses.title: A written treatment of a topic
senses.definition: a passage or chapter that examines a subject in writing
senses.definitionCN: 以书面形式考察某一主题的段落或章节
senses.example: The book opens with a discussion of early printing.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书以对早期印刷术的论述开篇。
senses.why: Writing can shake a subject apart too, only slowly and on the page. The noun transfers the conversational act to text without changing its core.
senses.whyCN: 写作也能把话题摇散，只是慢一些，而且在纸面上。这个名词把交谈行为搬到文本上，核心未变。

senses.title: The section after results
senses.definition: in a research paper, the section that interprets results and relates them to earlier work
senses.definitionCN: 研究论文中解释结果并将其与先前研究联系起来的章节
senses.example: The discussion admits that the sample was small.
senses.exampleCN: 讨论部分承认样本规模较小。
senses.why: The section is where results are turned over and weighed. Its name is fixed by academic convention, but the metaphor of examining from several sides still holds.
senses.whyCN: 这一节正是结果被翻过来权衡的地方。这个名称由学术惯例固定，但“从多面考察”的比喻仍然成立。

senses.title: Negotiating terms between parties
senses.definition: a series of talks aimed at reaching agreement or settling terms
senses.definitionCN: 旨在达成一致或确定条款的一系列会谈
senses.example: The two sides held discussions in Geneva.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在日内瓦举行了商议。
senses.why: Here the subject being shaken apart is a proposed deal. The plural is common because negotiation usually takes several sessions.
senses.whyCN: 这里被摇散的对象是一份拟议的交易。复数很常见，因为谈判通常要谈好几轮。

senses.title: Being considered at the moment
senses.definition: the state of being under consideration, as in the phrase under discussion
senses.definitionCN: 处于考虑之中的状态，如短语 under discussion
senses.example: The proposal under discussion would cut the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 正在讨论的提案将削减预算。
senses.why: The preposition turns the act into a location: the topic currently sits on the table. English often uses spatial phrases for topics in progress.
senses.whyCN: 介词把行为变成位置：这个话题此刻摆在桌上。英语常用空间短语表示进行中的议题。

senses.title: An online thread of replies
senses.definition: a public exchange of messages on a forum or message board
senses.definitionCN: 在论坛或留言板上公开往来的信息串
senses.example: The discussion ran to two hundred replies.
senses.exampleCN: 这个讨论帖有两百条回复。
senses.why: Digital discussion keeps the turns but loses the table. It is still a shaking-apart, now asynchronous and recorded.
senses.whyCN: 网络讨论保留了轮次，却失去了桌子。它仍是摇散，只是异步且被记录。

senses.title: A method of teaching by talk
senses.definition: in education, a planned classroom exchange used to develop understanding
senses.definitionCN: 教育中为发展理解而设计的课堂交流
senses.example: Guided discussion improved the students' reasoning.
senses.exampleCN: 有引导的讨论提高了学生的推理能力。
senses.why: The method assumes understanding is built by turning a problem over aloud. Discussion becomes a technique with rules, not just talk.
senses.whyCN: 这种方法假定理解是靠出声翻动问题建立起来的。讨论于是成了有规则的技术，而不只是聊天。

senses.title: A public panel on a stage
senses.definition: a public event in which several speakers discuss a topic before an audience
senses.definitionCN: 数位讲者在观众面前讨论某一话题的公开活动
senses.example: The festival hosted a panel discussion on AI and art.
senses.exampleCN: 该节庆举办了一场关于人工智能与艺术的小组讨论。
senses.why: Here discussion is a performance with a stage and an audience. The exchange is real, but it is also arranged for listeners.
senses.whyCN: 这里的讨论是有舞台、有观众的一场表演。交流是真实的，但也是为听众安排的。

intro.en: Discussion is Latin discussio from discutere, dis- 'apart' plus quatere 'to shake'. The Latin verb meant 'to strike asunder, to examine'. English took the noun through French in the 15th century, and the modern conversational sense settled later.
intro.cn: discussion 是拉丁 discussio，来自 discutere，即 dis-“分开”加 quatere“摇动”。这个拉丁动词意为“打散、审查”。英语在 15 世纪经法语借入名词，现代的交谈义后来才稳定。

items.en: The root *kwet- meant 'to shake'. Latin quatere comes from it, and so do quash and the -cuss- of concussion and percussion.
items.cn: 词根 *kwet- 意为“摇动”。拉丁 quatere 由此而来，quash 以及 concussion、percussion 中的 -cuss- 也同出此源。

items.en: Quatere meant 'to shake, to strike'. With dis- it became discutere, 'to strike apart, to shake to pieces', and then figuratively 'to examine, to debate'.
items.cn: quatere 意为“摇、击”。加 dis- 成为 discutere“打散、震碎”，再引申为“审查、辩论”。

items.en: The noun discussio named a shaking apart and, in later Latin, an investigation. Legal writers used it for the examination of a case.
items.cn: 名词 discussio 指震散，晚期拉丁中也指调查。法律作家用它指对案件的审查。

items.en: French discussion entered English in the 15th century with the sense 'examination, debate'. The modern conversational sense is common by the 17th century.
items.cn: 法语 discussion 于 15 世纪进入英语，意为“审查、辩论”。现代的交谈义在 17 世纪已常见。

items.en: Scientific writing fixes the discussion section as the place where results are interpreted, giving the word a structural role in papers.
items.cn: 科学写作把讨论部分固定为解释结果的所在，使这个词在论文中获得结构性角色。

items.en: Panel discussions, classroom discussion and online discussion extend the word to formats. The core action remains the same: turning a subject over together.
items.cn: 小组讨论、课堂讨论与网络讨论把这个词扩展到各种形式。核心动作仍是同一个：一起把话题翻过来看。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the conference role and a same-root adjective. The meaning group contrasts discussion with debate, conversation and negotiation.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、会议角色与同词根形容词；词义组把讨论与辩论、交谈、谈判区分开。

entries.definition: to talk over a subject. The noun adds -ion to this verb.
entries.definitionCN: 讨论某一话题。名词在其上加 -ion。

entries.definition: a person who comments on papers at a symposium. It names a role, not the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 在研讨会上对论文作评论的人。它指角色，而非活动。

entries.definition: rambling, or proceeding by argument rather than intuition. It descends from the same verb but no longer means discussion.
entries.definitionCN: 散漫的，或依论证而非直觉进行的。它同出该动词，但已不再表示“讨论”。

entries.definition: an informal exchange between people. It need not have a topic or a purpose, while a discussion usually has both.
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间非正式的交流。它不必有话题或目的，而讨论通常两者都有。

entries.definition: a formal argument between opposing sides. It requires sides; a discussion does not.
entries.definitionCN: 对立双方之间的正式论证。它要求有双方，讨论则不必。

entries.definition: talks aimed at an agreement. It is a specialised form of discussion with an outcome to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 以达成协议为目标的会谈。它是讨论的一种专门形式，有必须达到的结果。

entries.definition: careful consideration before a decision. It is slower and more formal than discussion and aims at a verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 决定前的仔细权衡。它比讨论更慢、更正式，并以裁决为目标。

entries.definition: a running explanation of a text or event. It is one-directional, while discussion expects replies.
entries.definitionCN: 对文本或事件的连续解说。它是单向的，而讨论期待回应。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the physical root 'to shake' in view, then let the same shaking happen at a table, on a page and on a screen.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把“摇动”这个物理词根放在眼前，再让同一种摇动发生在桌上、纸上与屏幕上。

normal.en: See dis- + quatere: to shake apart. Discussion shakes a topic to see inside.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 quatere：摇散。discussion 把话题摇开看里面。

normal.en: Picture four people turning a report over and over on a round table.
normal.cn: 想象四个人在圆桌上把一份报告翻来翻去。

normal.en: For a paper, the discussion is where results get turned over and weighed.
normal.cn: 论文里，讨论部分正是结果被翻过来权衡的地方。

normal.en: Keep the pair: debate needs sides, discussion needs only a topic.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：debate 需要有双方，discussion 只需有话题。

normal.en: For online threads, the table is gone but the turns remain.
normal.cn: 网络帖子方面，桌子没了，轮次还在。

abstract.en: Reduce every sense to one motion: a subject is turned to show its other faces.
abstract.cn: 把每个义项缩成一个动作：话题被翻面，露出它的其他面。

abstract.en: Notice that discussion is cooperative shaking; it is not the same as knocking something down.
abstract.cn: 注意讨论是合作的摇动，它与把东西击倒不同。

abstract.en: Ask of each use: who is holding the topic, and who is allowed to turn it?
abstract.cn: 对每个用法都问：谁握着话题，谁有权把它翻面？

examples.en: After much discussion, the committee voted to postpone.
examples.cn: 经过充分讨论，委员会投票决定推迟。

examples.en: The paper's discussion section is longer than its results.
examples.cn: 这篇论文的讨论部分比结果部分还长。

examples.en: The question remains under discussion.
examples.cn: 这个问题仍在讨论中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯库申”：地斯库（discuss）把一口锅摇得哐当作响，大家围着锅边摇边谈——discussion 就是讨论。

root: 拉丁语 quatere“摇动、击打”，加 dis- 成 discutere“打散、审查”，名词 discussio；经法语 discussion 于 15 世纪进入英语。同根词有 concussion、percussion、quash、rescue（excutere）。

sensesIntro.en: Discussion is a Latin verb for shaking something apart. At a table, two or three people shake a topic until its parts show; in a paper, the same shaking happens on the page; in a negotiation, the thing shaken is a draft agreement; online, the shaking is recorded in a thread. The nine senses differ in medium and formality, not in the core motion.
sensesIntro.cn: discussion 是一个表示“把东西摇散”的拉丁动词。在桌旁，两三个人把话题摇到各部分露出来；在论文里，同样的摇动发生在纸面上；在谈判中，被摇的是一份协议草案；在网上，这次摇动被记录成一串回复。九个义项在介质与正式程度上不同，核心动作则相同。

core.en: Shaking a subject apart together so that its parts can be seen.
core.cn: 一起把话题摇散，使各部分可见。

branches.en: TALK: everyday conversation and its online thread.
branches.cn: 交谈：日常对话及其网络帖子。

branches.en: FORUM: expert seminars and public panels.
branches.cn: 论坛：专家研讨与公开小组讨论。

branches.en: TEXT: written treatment and the paper's discussion section.
branches.cn: 文本：书面论述与论文的讨论部分。

branches.en: NEGOTIATION: talks between parties, and the state of being under consideration.
branches.cn: 谈判：各方会谈，以及处于考虑之中的状态。

branches.en: TEACHING: planned classroom exchange.
branches.cn: 教学：有设计的课堂交流。

intro.en: Discussion is dis- plus a shaking verb plus -ion. The items show that the same quatere root gives words of impact, which is why discussion once meant 'to strike apart'.
intro.cn: discussion 是 dis- 加“摇动”动词再加 -ion。下列条目展示同一 quatere 词根给出表示撞击的词，这正是 discussion 曾意为“打散”的原因。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are the shaking verb, its compound and its noun. They make the original violence of the metaphor visible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出摇动的动词、其复合形式与名词。它们让这个比喻原本的“暴力”变得可见。

items.meaning: an exchange of views; a written treatment
items.example: The discussion lasted two hours.
We discussed the plan over lunch.
items.exampleCN: 我们午餐时讨论了计划。

items.meaning: one who comments on a paper
items.example: The discussant raised two objections.
The essay is discursive rather than linear.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章是发散式的，而非线性的。

items.meaning: a violent shaking, especially of the brain
items.example: He suffered a mild concussion.
The percussion section opened the piece.
items.exampleCN: 打击乐声部开启了这首曲子。

items.example: The court quashed the verdict.
They rescued the climbers at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 他们在黎明时营救了登山者。

items.example: Squash the garlic with a knife.

definition_zh: 位移；取代；流离失所；排水量；（心理）置换；（引擎）排量
definition_en: the act of moving something from its place, the amount moved, or the replacement of one thing by another
core_image: 把一本书从书架的固定位置抽走，留下一个空的缺口，旁边的人把另一本书塞了进去
scene: 书架上，管理员抽走一本书，留下空位，又把另一本放进同一格：the displacement of one volume by another。
sceneCN: 这里 displacement 是「移走、取代」（第 1、2 个义项：离开原位与取代）；句意：一本被移走，另一本占了它的位置。图中可辨识物件：书架、空出的格位、两本书、梯凳。

pos.zh: 位移；取代；流离失所；排水量；置换

derivatives.zh: 放置；安置（同词根，方向相反）

senses.title: Moving something out of its place
senses.definition: the act of moving an object from the position it occupied
senses.definitionCN: 把物体从其占据的位置移开的行为
senses.example: The displacement of the statue required a crane.
senses.exampleCN: 移动这座雕像需要起重机。
senses.why: Dis- removes and place holds the position. Displacement is the undoing of placement: what was set here is now somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: dis- 表示移走，place 表示位置。displacement 是对 placement 的撤销：原本安放在此的东西现在在别处。

senses.title: Taking someone's role or place
senses.definition: the replacement of one person or thing by another that takes over its function
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或事物被另一个接管其功能的替换
senses.example: The displacement of hand tools by machines changed the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 机器对手工工具的取代改变了作坊。
senses.why: Here the thing moved is not the object but the occupant. One occupant is pushed out and another takes the slot, so the word describes replacement through eviction.
senses.whyCN: 这里被移走的不是物体，而是占据者。一个占据者被挤出，另一个占了格子，因此这个词描述的是“通过逐出实现的替换”。

senses.title: A change of position in physics
senses.definition: in physics, the vector distance and direction from an initial to a final position
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中从初始位置到末位置的距离与方向矢量
senses.example: The displacement is zero when the runner returns to the start.
senses.exampleCN: 跑者回到起点时位移为零。
senses.why: Physics separates distance travelled from displacement achieved. The word measures where you ended relative to where you began, not how far you walked.
senses.whyCN: 物理学区分走过的距离与达成的位移。这个词衡量的是你相对起点落在哪里，而不是你走了多远。

senses.title: Water pushed aside by a body
senses.definition: the volume or weight of fluid moved out of the way by a floating or submerged object
senses.definitionCN: 浮体或浸没物体排开的流体体积或重量
senses.example: The ship has a displacement of forty thousand tonnes.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船的排水量为四万吨。
senses.why: An object cannot enter water without water leaving. Displacement names that forced removal, and Archimedes turned it into a measure of the object.
senses.whyCN: 物体进入水中，水必然离开。displacement 命名这种被迫的移走，阿基米德把它变成对物体的度量。

senses.title: Redirecting a feeling onto a safer target
senses.definition: in psychoanalysis, the transfer of an emotion from its original object to a substitute
senses.definitionCN: 精神分析中把情感从原对象转移到替代对象
senses.example: Anger at the boss found displacement onto a colleague.
senses.exampleCN: 对上司的怒气被置换到同事身上。
senses.why: The feeling is moved out of its proper place and lodged somewhere else. The word keeps its spatial sense while the thing displaced becomes an emotion.
senses.whyCN: 情感被移离其应在的位置，安放到别处。这个词在空间义不变的情况下，被移动的东西变成了情感。

senses.title: Language about what is not here
senses.definition: in linguistics, the capacity of language to refer to things absent in time or space
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中语言指称时间或空间中不在场之物的能力
senses.example: Displacement lets a speaker discuss last winter in June.
senses.exampleCN: 位移性让说话者在六月谈论去年冬天。
senses.why: Words travel away from the here and now. This sense treats the whole language system as the thing displaced from its immediate setting.
senses.whyCN: 词语离开此时此地。这个义项把整个语言系统看作从当下情境中被移走的东西。

senses.title: Rock moved along a fault
senses.definition: in geology, the relative movement of rock on either side of a fault
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中断层两侧岩石的相对移动
senses.example: The fault shows a displacement of several metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这条断层显示出数米的位移。
senses.why: The ground itself has been moved out of place. The sense is literal: two blocks that once matched no longer line up.
senses.whyCN: 地面本身被移离了原位。这个义项是字面的：原本对得上的两块岩石不再对齐。

senses.title: One element pushing another out
senses.definition: in chemistry, a reaction in which one element displaces another from a compound
senses.definitionCN: 化学中一种元素把另一种元素从化合物中置换出来
senses.example: Zinc displacement of copper turns the solution colourless.
senses.exampleCN: 锌置换铜使溶液褪色。
senses.why: An atom is evicted from its place in a molecule by a more reactive rival. The competition for a position is the same image as sense 02.
senses.whyCN: 一个原子被更具反应性的对手从分子中的位置挤出。为位置而竞争，与第 2 义项是同一个意象。

senses.title: The swept volume of an engine
senses.definition: the total volume swept by the pistons of an engine in one complete cycle
senses.definitionCN: 发动机活塞在一个完整循环中扫过的总体积
senses.example: A larger displacement gives more torque but uses more fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 更大的排量带来更大扭矩，但更费油。
senses.why: Each piston pushes air out of the space it occupies, exactly as a body pushes water aside. Engine displacement is the same measure applied to cylinders.
senses.whyCN: 每个活塞把它占据的空间里的空气推出去，正如物体排开水。发动机排量就是把同一度量用在气缸上。

intro.en: Displacement is displace plus -ment. Place goes back to Latin platea, 'broad street', from Greek plateia, from platys 'broad'. Displace means to remove from a place, and the noun names that removal and its measure.
intro.cn: displacement 是 displace 加 -ment。place 上溯拉丁 platea“宽阔的街道”，再上溯希腊 plateia，词根 platys“宽阔”。displace 意为移离某处，名词命名这种移离及其度量。

items.en: Platys meant 'broad, flat'. The feminine plateia named a broad way or square. The same root gives plate, plateau and platypus, literally 'flat-foot'.
items.cn: platys 意为“宽阔、扁平”。阴性形式 plateia 指宽路或广场。同一词根给出 plate、plateau，以及字面为“扁足”的 platypus。

items.en: Latin platea took the Greek word for a broad street. It was used for open squares in Roman towns and passed into the everyday speech of the provinces.
items.cn: 拉丁 platea 借入这个表示宽街的希腊词。它用于罗马城镇的广场，并进入各行省的日常口语。

items.en: Old French place meant 'open space, position'. English borrowed it twice: once through French, once directly from Latin in learned words such as plaza.
items.cn: 古法语 place 意为“开阔空间、位置”。英语两次借用：一次经法语，一次在 plaza 等学术词中直接借自拉丁。

items.en: English place settles as 'a particular position or locality'. The verb to place, 'to put in a position', follows, and with it the noun placement.
items.cn: 英语 place 稳定为“特定位置或地点”。动词 to place“安置”随之而来，名词 placement 也一并出现。

items.en: Displace is formed with dis- to mean 'remove from its place, put out of office'. The nautical sense of a ship's displacement appears in the 18th century.
items.cn: displace 由 dis- 构成，意为“移离原位、撤职”。船舶排水量的航海义在 18 世纪出现。

items.en: Physics fixes displacement as a vector; geology and chemistry adopt the term; psychoanalysis borrows it for a defence mechanism in the early 20th century.
items.cn: 物理学把 displacement 固定为矢量；地质学与化学采用该词；精神分析在 20 世纪初借它指一种防御机制。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the adjective of people and the noun of putting in place. The meaning group contrasts displacement with replacement, migration and substitution.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、描述人的形容词与“安放”名词；词义组把 displacement 与替换、迁徙、代替区分开。

entries.definition: to move out of place, or to take over the role of. The noun adds -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 移离原位，或取代某物的角色。名词加 -ment。

entries.definition: forced to leave home or position. It describes the people affected, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 被迫离开家园或职位的。它描述受影响的人，而非过程。

entries.definition: the act of putting someone or something in a position. Displacement undoes it.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物放到某位置的行为。displacement 撤销它。

entries.definition: the act of putting something new in the place of another. It stresses the newcomer; displacement stresses the one pushed out.
entries.definitionCN: 把新物放到另一物位置的行为。它强调新来者，displacement 强调被挤出者。

entries.definition: movement from one region to another, often seasonal or voluntary. Displacement usually implies compulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个地区到另一个地区的移动，常为季节性或自愿。displacement 通常含被迫之意。

entries.definition: the legal removal of a tenant from property. It is one concrete mechanism of displacement.
entries.definitionCN: 依法把租户从房产中逐出。它是 displacement 的一种具体机制。

entries.definition: the use of one thing in place of another. It is neutral about whether anyone was pushed out.
entries.definitionCN: 用一物代替另一物。它对是否有人被挤出保持中立。

entries.definition: a turning aside from a straight path. It describes a change of direction, while displacement describes a change of position.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离直线路径。它描述方向改变，而 displacement 描述位置改变。

normalIntro.en: These hooks hold the image of a vacated slot, then apply it to objects, people, water, feelings and atoms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩抓住“空出的格子”这个意象，再把它用到物体、人、水、情感与原子上。

normal.en: See dis- + place: the thing is taken out of its place.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 place：东西被拿出原位。

normal.en: Picture the empty shelf slot, then someone else filling it. That is replacement by displacement.
normal.cn: 想象书架上空出的格位，随后被别人填上。这就是通过移走实现的替换。

normal.en: In physics, ask only two questions: where did it start, where did it end?
normal.cn: 物理方面只问两个问题：从哪开始，在哪结束？

normal.en: For ships, the hull cannot enter without water leaving. That leaving water is the displacement.
normal.cn: 船方面，船体进不去水不出去。离开的那些水就是排水量。

normal.en: For psychology, the feeling is moved to a safer chair in the room.
normal.cn: 心理学方面，情感被挪到房间里更安全的一把椅子上。

abstract.en: Reduce every sense to one operation: something occupies a slot, then does not.
abstract.cn: 把每个义项缩成一个操作：某物占据一个格子，然后不再占据。

abstract.en: Notice the double edge: displacement is both a move and a loss of position.
abstract.cn: 注意它的双刃：displacement 既是移动，也是失去位置。

abstract.en: Ask of each use: is the thing moved, or is the thing taking its place the focus?
abstract.cn: 对每个用法都问：焦点是被移走的东西，还是接替它的那个？

examples.en: The war caused the displacement of millions of people.
examples.cn: 战争造成数百万人流离失所。

examples.en: Measure the displacement of the trolley from its starting mark.
examples.cn: 测量小车相对起始标记的位移。

examples.en: Automation has displaced many routine jobs.
examples.cn: 自动化取代了许多常规工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯普雷斯门特”：地斯普雷斯（displace）的门被移走了，门一移、位置一空，就是位移与取代。

root: 希腊语 platys“宽阔”，阴性 plateia 指宽路；拉丁 platea“宽街、广场”；经古法语 place 进入英语作 place“位置”，加 dis- 构成 displace“移离原位”，再加 -ment 构成 displacement。同根词有 place、plate、plateau、plaza。

sensesIntro.en: Displacement is the negative of placement: something that was put here is no longer here. The thing removed can be an object, an occupant, a body of water, an emotion, a reference in time, a block of rock, an atom or a volume of air. In each case the word measures the same event, a slot that is now occupied differently or left empty.
sensesIntro.cn: displacement 是 placement 的反面：原本放在这里的东西不再在这里。被移走的可以是物体、占据者、一团水、一种情感、一个时间指称、一块岩石、一个原子或一团空气。每一种情况下，这个词衡量的都是同一件事：一个格子如今被别样占据，或空了出来。

core.en: A vacated slot: what was in place is moved or replaced.
core.cn: 空出的格子：本在位的东西被移走或替换。

branches.en: SPACE: objects moved, vectors measured, rock offset along a fault.
branches.cn: 空间：物体被移、矢量被量、岩石沿断层错动。

branches.en: COMPETITION: an occupant evicted by a rival, in work or in chemistry.
branches.cn: 竞争：占据者被对手挤出，在职场或在化学中。

branches.en: VOLUME: water pushed aside, air swept by pistons.
branches.cn: 体积：被推开的水，被活塞扫过的空气。

branches.en: MIND: a feeling lodged on a substitute target.
branches.cn: 心理：情感被安放到替代目标上。

branches.en: LANGUAGE: words referring beyond the here and now.
branches.cn: 语言：词语指称此时此地之外。

intro.en: Displacement is dis- plus place plus -ment. The items show both directions of the place family: placement puts in, displacement takes out, replacement puts back.
intro.cn: displacement 是 dis- 加 place 再加 -ment。下列条目展示 place 词族的两个方向：placement 放进去，displacement 拿出来，replacement 放回去。

latinIntro.en: The Latin and Greek entries show that place was originally a broad street, not an abstract point. The word still carries that sense of an open space someone can occupy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁与希腊语条目说明 place 原本是一条宽街，而不是抽象的点。这个词仍带着“可供占据的开阔空间”之意。

items.meaning: the act or amount of moving out of place
items.example: The displacement of the population was sudden.

items.meaning: to move out of position; to supplant
items.example: The new system displaced the old one.

items.meaning: forced out of home or position
items.meaningCN: 被迫离开家园或职位的
items.example: Aid reached the displaced families.
items.exampleCN: 援助送到了流离失所的家庭。

items.meaning: the act of putting in position
items.example: The placement of the sign was poor.
items.exampleCN: 这块牌子的位置放得不好。

items.meaning: to put back; to take the place of
items.example: Replace the lid after use.

items.meaning: to put in the wrong place; to lose temporarily
items.example: I misplaced the keys again.

items.structure: Old French plate, from Latin platea
items.example: The armour plate weighed heavily.

items.meaning: a flat raised area of land
items.example: The herd grazed on the plateau.
The market fills the plaza on Sundays.

definition_zh: 独特的；有辨识度的；区别性的；特有的
definition_en: serving to distinguish something, or so characteristic that it is easily recognized
core_image: 一群相似的鸟里，有一只胸前的红斑独一无二
scene: 观鸟台上，一群人举着望远镜，指向一只胸前有红斑的鸟。On the birdwatching platform a group points through binoculars at a bird with a distinctive red patch on its breast.
sceneCN: 这里 distinctive 是「有辨识度的、独特的」（第 1、2 个义项：区别作用与易于辨认）；句意：观鸟台上，一群人举着望远镜指向一只胸前有独特红斑的鸟。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、鸟群、胸前的红斑、图鉴。

pos.zh: 独特的；区别性的；有辨识度的

senses.title: Serving to tell one thing from another
senses.definition: marking a difference that allows one thing to be told apart from others
senses.definitionCN: 标示出某种差异，使一物能与别的区分开
senses.example: The distinctive feature of the species is its curved bill.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种的显著特征是弯喙。
senses.why: Latin distinguere is dis- 'apart' plus stinguere 'to prick'. A distinctive mark is a pricked line that separates one thing from the next.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 distinguere 是 dis-“分开”加 stinguere“刺”。distinctive 的标记就是一条刺出来的线，把一物与下一物分开。

senses.title: Easy to recognize at once
senses.definition: so characteristic that it can be recognized quickly and confidently
senses.definitionCN: 特征明显到能被迅速且确信地认出
senses.example: She has a distinctive way of laughing.
senses.exampleCN: 她笑起来的方式很有辨识度。
senses.why: Recognition is the practical test of a distinction. If the mark lets you pick the right one without hesitation, it is distinctive.
senses.whyCN: 认出是区分是否有效的实际检验。如果这个标记让你毫不犹豫地挑对，它就是有辨识度的。

senses.title: Belonging to one person or place
senses.definition: characteristic of a particular individual, group or region rather than of a whole class
senses.definitionCN: 属于特定个人、群体或地区而非整个类别的
senses.example: The valley has a distinctive microclimate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷有独特的小气候。
senses.why: A distinction can be collective. The adjective then says that this feature belongs here and is not shared with neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 区分也可以是集体的。此时形容词表示这个特征属于此地，并不与邻处共享。

senses.title: A sound that changes meaning
senses.titleCN: 区别性语音特征（语言学）
senses.definition: in phonology, describing a sound feature that distinguishes one phoneme from another in a language
senses.definitionCN: 音系学中描述能在一门语言里把一个音位与另一个区分开的语音特征
senses.example: Voicing is a distinctive feature in English.
senses.exampleCN: 清浊对立在英语中是区别性特征。
senses.why: Phonology borrows the word for a formal job: if swapping the feature changes the word, the feature is distinctive; if not, it is not.
senses.whyCN: 音系学借这个词给一项形式化工作命名：若替换该特征会改变词义，它就是区别性的；若不会，就不是。

senses.title: A strength rivals cannot copy
senses.definition: in business strategy, describing a capability that sets a firm apart and is hard for rivals to imitate
senses.definitionCN: 战略管理中描述使公司与众不同且难以被对手模仿的能力
senses.example: Their distinctive competence is rapid prototyping.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的独特能力是快速原型开发。
senses.why: A firm survives by being separable from the crowd. Distinctive competence is the internal mark that makes the separation real rather than advertised.
senses.whyCN: 公司靠与众人可分开而存活。独特能力就是那个使分离成为真实而非广告说辞的内部标记。

senses.title: A mark that can be a trademark
senses.definition: in trademark law, describing a sign that consumers can use to identify the source of goods
senses.definitionCN: 商标法中描述消费者能借以识别商品来源的标志
senses.example: The court found the logo sufficiently distinctive.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定该标识具有足够的显著性。
senses.why: A trademark must do the work of a distinction: tell this seller's goods from another's. Generic words cannot, so distinctiveness is a legal threshold.
senses.whyCN: 商标必须承担区分的工作：把这家的货与别家的分开。通用词做不到，因此显著性是法律门槛。

senses.title: Markings that identify an animal
senses.definition: in zoology, describing patterns or features by which individuals or species are identified
senses.definitionCN: 动物学中描述用于识别个体或物种的纹样或特征
